前言

Preface

不久前，市面上几乎没有关于面向对象分析与设计的书籍。如今，这类书籍汗牛充栋，任何从业者都难以全部阅读。大多数书籍侧重于讲解某种符号体系，提出一种简单的建模流程，并用几个简单的例子加以说明。《分析模式：可重用对象模型》则截然不同。它并非着眼于建模过程（如何建模），而是聚焦于建模的结果——模型本身。

Not long ago, no books were available on object-oriented analysis and design. Now there are so many that it is impossible for any practitioner to keep up with them all. Most of these books concentrate on teaching a notation, suggesting a simple process for modeling, and illustrating it with a few simple examples. Analysis Patterns: Reusable Object Models is a different kind of book. Instead of focusing on the process—how to do modeling—it concentrates on the result of the process—the models themselves.

我是一名信息系统对象建模顾问。客户会邀请我培训员工进行建模，并为项目提供指导。我的技​​能主要来源于对建模技术及其应用的了解。然而，更重要的是我拥有丰富的实际模型创建经验，并且经常发现问题会反复出现。我经常发现，项目的许多方面都会重现我之前遇到的问题。这些经验使我能够重用之前构建的模型，对其进行改进，并使其适应新的需求。

I am a consultant in object modeling for information systems. Clients ask me to train staff on modeling and to provide mentoring on projects. Much of my skill comes from a knowledge of modeling techniques and how to use them. More important, however, is my experience in actually creating many models and regularly seeing problems repeat themselves. Frequently I find that many aspects of a project revisit problems I have faced before. That experience allows me to reuse models I have built before, improve them, and adapt them to new demands.

近年来，越来越多的人开始意识到这种现象。我们认识到，传统的方法论书籍虽然很有价值，但仅仅展现了学习过程的第一步，而学习过程还必须涵盖实际构建的内容。这种认识催生了模式运动。这是一个多元化的群体，成员们代表着不同的兴趣和观点，但他们共同的目标是传播有用的软件系统模式。

Over the last few years, more and more people have also become aware of this phenomenon. We have realized that the typical methodology books, though valuable, only present the first step in a learning process that must also capture the actual things that are built. This realization has flowered into the patterns movement. This is a varied group of people, representing many different interests and opinions yet sharing the goal of propagating useful patterns of software systems.

由于模式社群的多样性，我们一直难以定义“模式”一词。我们都认为自己能够识别模式，而且在大多数情况下，大多数人都会认同这一点，但我们却无法给出一个统一的定义。以下是我的定义：模式是指在某个实际情境中行之有效，并且很可能在其他情境中也同样有效的理念。

As a result of the diversity of this patterns community, we have had difficulty in defining the term pattern. We all think we can recognize a pattern when we see it, we think most of us would agree in most cases, but we cannot come up with a single definition. Here is my definition: A pattern is an idea that has been useful in one practical context and will probably be useful in others.

我喜欢对模式的定义保持一定的宽泛性，因为我希望尽可能贴近模式的根本动机，而避免添加过多限制性的修正。模式可以有多种形式，每种形式都会增加一些对该类型模式有用的特殊功能。（1.2 节讨论了模式领域的现状以及本书的定位。）

I like to leave the definition quite loose because I wish to stay as close to the underlying motivation of patterns, without adding too many restrictive amendments. A pattern can have many forms, and each form adds specializations that are useful for that kind of pattern. (Section 1.2 discusses the current state of the patterns world and where this book fits in.)

本书探讨的是分析模式，这些模式反映的是业务流程的概念结构，而非实际的软件实现。大部分章节讨论了各个业务领域的模式。这些模式很难归入传统的垂直领域（例如制造业、金融业、医疗保健业等），因为它们通常在多个领域都适用。这些模式之所以重要，是因为它们有助于我们理解人们如何感知世界。基于这种感知来设计计算机系统，甚至改变这种感知——这正是业务流程重组（BPR）的意义所在——都具有重要价值。

This book is about patterns in analysis, patterns that reflect conceptual structures of business processes rather than actual software implementations. Most of the chapters discuss patterns for various business domains. Such patterns are hard to classify into traditional vertical areas (manufacturing, finance, health care, and so on) because they are often useful in several areas. These patterns are important because they help us to understand how people perceive the world. It is valuable to base a computer system's design on this perception and, indeed, to change that perception—which is where business process reengineering (BPR) comes in.

然而，概念模式并非孤立存在。只有当软件工程师能够理解如何实现概念模型时，它们才能发挥作用。本书介绍了一些可用于将概念模型转化为软件的模式，并探讨了这些软件如何融入大型信息系统的架构。此外，本书还分享了一些具体的模式实现技巧。

Conceptual patterns cannot exist in isolation, however. Conceptual models are only useful to software engineers if they can see how to implement them. In this book I present patterns that can be used to turn conceptual models into software, and I discuss how that software fits into an architecture for a large information system. I also discuss specific implementation tips with the patterns.

我写这本书是因为我当初入行时就想读这样的书。建模人员可以从本书中找到灵感，帮助他们在新领域开展工作。书中的模式包含实用的模型、模型背后的设计原理，以及适用和不适用的场景。有了这些信息，建模人员可以根据具体问题调整模型。

I wrote this book because this was the book that I wanted to read when I started out. Modelers will find ideas in this book to help them begin working in a new domain. The patterns contain useful models, the reasoning behind their designs, and when they should and should not be applied. With this information a modeler can adapt the models to fit a specific problem.

本书中的模式也可用于模型审查——查看可能遗漏的内容，并提出一些可能改进的替代方案。在审查项目时，我通常会将所见与我从以往工作中学到的模式进行比较。我发现，了解工作中的模式有助于我更轻松地应用过去的经验。这类模式还能揭示一些超出简单教科书范围的建模问题。通过探讨我们为何以这种方式建模，即使我们不直接使用这些模式，也能更深入地理解如何改进建模。

The patterns in this book can also be used in reviewing models—to see what might have been left out and to suggest some alternatives that may lead to improvement. When I review a project, I usually compare what I see with the patterns I have learned from previous work. I have found that being aware of patterns in my work helps me to apply my past experiences more easily. Patterns like this also uncover modeling issues that go beyond what can be covered in a simple text book. By discussing why we model things the way we do, we gain a greater understanding of how to improve our modeling, even if we don't use the patterns directly.

本书结构分为两部分。第一部分涵盖分析模式，这些模式源自概念性商业模型。它们提供了交易、计量、会计和组织关系等领域的关键抽象概念。这些模式是概念性的，因为它们代表了人们对业务的思考方式，而非计算机系统的设计方式。本部分各章节重点介绍可用的替代模式，以及这些替代模式的优缺点。虽然每种模式对于从事同一领域工作的人员来说都非常有用，但基本模式通常也适用于其他领域。

Structure of this Book This book is divided into two sections. The first section covers analysis patterns, which are patterns from conceptual business models. They provide key abstractions from domains such as trading, measurement, accounting, and organizational relationships. The patterns are conceptual because they represent the way people think about the business, rather than the way a computer system is designed. The chapters in this section stress alternative patterns that can be used, and the strengths and weaknesses of those alternatives. Although each pattern will clearly be useful to those working in the same domain, the basic pattern is often useful in other domains.

第二部分重点介绍支持模式，它能帮助您使用分析模式。支持模式展示了分析模式如何融入信息系统架构，概念模型的结构如何转化为软件接口和实现，以及某些高级建模结构如何与更简单的结构相关联。

The second section focuses on support patterns, which help you use analysis patterns. Support patterns show how analysis patterns fit into an information systems architecture, how the constructs of conceptual models turn into software interfaces and implementations, and how certain advanced modeling constructs relate to simpler structures.

为了描述这些模式，我需要一套符号系统。附录简要讨论了我使用的符号系统及其含义。我并不只使用一种方法，而是倾向于融合不同方法的技巧。附录并非旨在提供技巧教程，而是提供一个概述并帮助您回忆相关内容。它还告诉您在哪里可以找到关于我所用技巧的教程。

To describe these patterns, I need a notation. The appendix provides a brief discussion of the notation I use and what the symbols mean. I do not use a single method but prefer to mix techniques from different methods. The appendix is not designed to be a tutorial on techniques, but it should provide an outline and refresh your memory. It also tells you where to find a tutorial on the techniques I use.

每个部分都分为若干章节。每个关于分析模式的章节都包含一些模式，这些模式在主题领域上存在一个大致的关联，并受到催生这些模式的项目的影响。这种组织方式体现了任何模式都必须源于实际应用这一事实。每个模式都出现在章节内的一个子章节中。我没有使用某些模式作者使用的正式标题（参见1.2.2节）。我尽可能以接近原始项目形式的方式来描述每个模式，并尽量减少抽象。我添加了示例来展示模式在其原始领域中的应用，并提出模式在其他领域中的应用可能性。模式的最大难点之一在于如何将其抽象到其他领域；我遵循的原则是，这应该留给读者自行探索（参见1.2.3节）。因此，本书更像是一个目录，而不是一本需要从头到尾阅读的书籍。我力求使每个章节都可以独立于其他章节阅读。 （但这并非总是可行。如果某一章节需要先阅读另一章节，我会在该章节的引言中说明。）每一章都有一个引言，解释该章节的一般主题领域，总结该章节中的模式，并说明这些模式源自哪些项目。

Each section is divided into chapters. Each chapter on analysis patterns contains patterns that are related by a loose notion of subject area, influenced by the projects that spawned them. This organization reflects the fact that any pattern must come from a practical context. Each pattern appears in its own subsection within a chapter. I do not use any of the formal headings for patterns that are used by some patterns authors (see Section 1.2.2). I describe each pattern in a form that is as close to the original project form as is reasonable, with a minimum of abstraction. I add examples to show the use of the pattern within its original domain and also to suggest how the pattern might be used in other domains. One of the greatest difficulties of patterns is abstracting them into other domains; I follow the principle that this should be left to the reader (see Section 1.2.3). This book is thus a catalog, rather than a book to be read from cover to cover. I have tried to write each chapter in such a way that it can be read independently from the other chapters. (This is not always possible, however. Whenever a chapter requires that another chapter be read first, I say so in the chapter introduction.) Each chapter has an introduction that explains the general subject area of the chapter, summarizes the patterns in the chapter, and says what projects the patterns originated from.

如何阅读本书？我建议您先通读第一章，然后再阅读各章的引言。之后，您可以随意选择阅读顺序。如果您不熟悉我的建模方法、符号和概念，请阅读附录。“模式表”简要概述了每种模式的内容，方便您日后查阅或探索书中的模式。需要强调的是，本书中的每种模式在其最初应用领域之外也同样适用。因此，我鼓励您阅读一些您认为与自身兴趣领域无关的章节。例如，我发现为医疗保健行业设计的观察和测量模型在企业财务分析中也同样适用。

How to Read this Book I suggest reading all of Chapter 1 first and then reading each chapter introduction. Then feel free to delve into the chapters in any order you like. If you are not familiar with the approach I take to modeling, or the notation and concepts I use, read the appendix. The Table of Patterns gives a brief summary of what each pattern is about, so you can use that to help you explore or to find a pattern when you come back to the book at a later time. It is important to stress that each pattern in this book is useful outside the domain that gave it birth. Thus I encourage you to look into chapters that you might think are outside your field of interest. For example, I found that models of observation and measurement designed for health care proved to be very useful for corporate financial analysis.

谁应该读这本书？ 这本书对很多读者都有用，尽管不同的读者会从中学到不同的东西，也可能需要一些不同的准备。

Who Should Read this Book This book can be useful to a range of readers, although different readers will learn different things from it and may need some different preparations.

我预计本书的主要读者是面向对象（OO）计算机系统的分析师和设计师，特别是那些从事分析工作的人员。这类读者应该至少对面向对象分析和设计方法有所了解。本书并未提供任何相关介绍，因此如果您是该领域的新手，我建议您先阅读一本关于面向对象分析和设计的书籍。我必须强调，本书中的模式本质上是概念性的，我采用的是一种非常概念化的建模方法。这导致本书在风格上与那些采用更注重实现的建模方法的书籍有所不同。

I expect my biggest audience to be analysts and designers of object-oriented (OO) computer systems, particularly those working at the analysis end. Such readers should have made at least some use of an OO analysis and design method. This book does not provide any introduction to this subject, so I would suggest first reading a book on OO analysis and design if you are new to this field. I must stress that the patterns in this book are conceptual in nature, and I use a very conceptual approach to modeling. This leads to some stylistic differences from those texts that use a more implementation-based approach to modeling.

本书的读者群体虽小，但却非常重要，他们是建模项目中的领域专家。这类读者无需具备计算机知识，但需要了解概念建模。我之所以在本书中使用概念模型，主要原因之一就是为了方便这类读者。这里的建模项目可以是计算机系统开发分析，也可以是业务流程重组（BPR）。我曾向许多专业人士（包括医生、金融交易员、会计师、护士和薪资主管）讲授过这类建模方法，发现软件背景对于概念建模而言既非优势也非劣势。业务模型模式既适用于业务建模，也适用于计算机系统分析（参见1.4节）。任何此类读者都应该参加一门强调概念方面的面向对象分析课程。（Odell 的著作[I]在这方面尤其有价值。）

A small, but very important, audience consists of those people who act as domain experts for a modeling project. Such readers do not require a knowledge of computers but do need to know about conceptual modeling. One of the main reasons I use conceptual models in this book is to make things easier for this group of readers. The modeling project here may be analysis for computer system development or BPR. I have taught many professionals (including doctors, financial traders, accountants, nurses, and payroll supervisors) this kind of modeling and have found that a software background is neither an advantage nor a disadvantage to conceptual modeling. The business model patterns are as much about business modeling as they are about computer systems analysis (see Section 1.4). Any such reader should take a course on OO analysis that stresses the conceptual aspect. (Odell's book [ I ] is particularly valuable in this respect.)

我希望许多程序员都能认真阅读本书，尽管有些程序员可能会对书中缺乏代码示例和偏重概念的论述方式感到不满。对于这些读者，我建议你们特别留意第14章，该章应该有助于解释概念模型与最终软件之间的关系。

I hope many programmers will delve between these covers, although some programmers may take exception to the lack of code and the conceptual slant. For these readers I suggest you take particular note of Chapter 14, which should help to explain the relationship between the conceptual models and the resulting software.

这是一本面向对象的书籍，我毫不犹豫地宣称，面向对象方法是开发软件的最佳途径。然而，这些模型主要是概念模型，而许多数据建模人员长期以来一直使用概念（或逻辑）模型。数据建模人员会发现其中许多模式很有用，尤其是在他们使用更高级的语义技术的情况下。这些模型的面向对象特性将揭示面向对象方法与传统方法之间的许多差异。我建议读者将本书与一本强调建模的概念方面以及面向对象与语义数据建模之间联系的面向对象分析书籍结合使用。

This is an object-oriented book, and I do not hesitate in proclaiming my belief that the object-oriented approach is the superior way to develop software. These models, however, are primarily conceptual models, and many data modelers have had a long tradition of using conceptual (or logical) models. Data modelers should find many of the patterns useful, particularly if they use more advanced semantic techniques. The object-oriented features of the models will reveal many of the differences between object-oriented and traditional approaches. I would encourage such readers to use this book in conjunction with an OO analysis book that stresses the conceptual side of modeling and the links between OO and semantic data modeling.

管理者会发现本书可作为开展发展活动的起点。从某种模式入手有助于明确目标，项目规划也能充分利用这些模式所勾勒出的广阔图景。

Managers will find the book useful as a starting point for development activity. Starting from a pattern can help to clarify goals, and project planning can take advantage of the broad ground that patterns map out.

我写这本书并非为了学生，而是为了专业的软件工程师。不过，我希望有些学生也能看看。我当初学习分析与设计时，发现很难，因为能借鉴的优秀案例很少，尤其是那些来自大学之外的实际案例。正如优秀的代码能让你学到很多编程知识一样，优秀的模型也能让你学到很多分析与设计知识。

I have not aimed this book at students. I've written it more for the professional software engineer. I hope, however, that some students will take a look. When I was learning analysis and design, I found it difficult because there were few good examples I could learn from, examples that came out of the world outside the university. Just as looking at good code can teach you a lot about programming, looking at good models can teach you a lot about analysis and design.

一本鲜活的书 我认识的每一位作者都面临着同样的困境：一旦书出版，就仿佛定型了。书的内容在读者群体中传播，但作者却很难表达自己的想法。我知道自己一直在不断学习，也确信这些学习会改变我的想法。我希望这些改变能够传递给我的读者。

A Living Book Every author I know shares a frustration: Once a book is published it is fixed. The book spreads its advice around the community, yet the author has little way of expressing changes. I know how much I keep learning, and I am sure this learning will modify my ideas. I want these changes to be passed on to my readers.

艾迪生-韦斯利出版社将为本书提供一个网站<http://www.aw.com/cp/fowler.html>，用于发布更多资料，以延续本书的生命力。目前我还不确定网站的具体内容，但我预计会包含以下几点：

With this book, Addison-Wesley will provide a web site <http:// www.aw.com/cp/fowler.html> which will be used to pass on further materials to keep this book alive. At this stage I am not sure exactly what it will contain, but I expect the following:

• 我在书中学到的任何关于图案的新知识。

• any new things I learn about the patterns in the book.

• 对本书相关问题的回答

• answers to questions about the book

• 其他人对这些模式的有用评论

• useful commentary from others about the patterns

• 我和其他人提出的新分析模式

• new analysis patterns by myself, and by others

• 当统一建模符号出现时（或者到那时叫什么名字），我将用新的符号重新绘制书中的所有图表，并将它们放到网站上。

• when the Unified Modeling Notation appears (or whatever it is called by then) I will redraw all the diagrams in the book in the new notation and put them on the site.

这个网站将作为本书的补充，请密切关注它，并利用它告诉我如何改进和发展本书中的想法。

This site will be a complement to the book, so keep an eye on it and use it to let me know how to improve and develop the ideas between these pages.

致谢 任何作者都应感谢众多帮助过他的人。本书尤其如此，因为其中许多模式都是在我的客户、同事和朋友的帮助下构建的。在此，我谨向以下人士致以诚挚的谢意，无论他们是直接提及还是默默付出。

Acknowledgments Any author is indebted to many others who help. For this book this is particularly true since so many of the patterns were built with the help of my cli ents, colleagues, and friends. I would like to give my sincere thanks to the following, both named and implied.

首先，吉姆·奥德尔是我职业生涯中不可或缺的一部分。他教会了我很多关于信息系统开发的知识，并且一直是我灵感的源泉，给予我很多有益的建议，还总能给我带来独特的幽默感。我可以毫不夸张地说，没有他的支持，这本书根本不可能问世。

First and foremost, Jim Odell has been an essential part of my career. He has taught me much about developing information systems and has been a constant source of inspiration, helpful advice, and strange humor. I can safely say that without his support this book would not have happened.

伦敦 Coopers & Lybrand 团队在早期工作中提供了很大帮助，并陪伴我们度过了许多在 Smithfield's 的夜晚。

The team at Coopers & Lybrand in London helped with much of the early work and helped pass many evenings at Smithfield's.

John Edwards 对我早期关于概念建模及其在软件开发中的作用的许多想法产生了影响，他还向我介绍了许多有趣的想法，包括 Christopher Alexander 的想法。

John Edwards formed many of my early ideas about conceptual modeling and its role in software development, as well as introducing me to many interesting ideas, including those of Christopher Alexander.

约翰·霍普敦促我先考虑领域，再考虑技术，并在我职业生涯的几个关键时刻对我施了有益的魔法。

John Hope urged me to think of the domain first and technology second, as well as casting a helpful spell at several key points in my career.

伦敦圣玛丽医院的医生汤姆·凯恩斯和马克·瑟兹与我合作开发了构成本书第二章、第三章和第八章基础的医疗保健模型。他们证明，计算机背景并非成为一流概念建模师的必要条件。马克还慷慨地提供了许多医疗保健案例，这些案例运用了听起来很专业的医学术语。

Tom Cairns and Mark Thursz, doctors at St. Mary's Hospital in London, worked with me in developing the health care models that form the basis of Chapters 2, 3, and 8. They are proof that a computer background is not necessary to be a top-class conceptual modeler. Mark also was a willing source for health care examples with impressive-sounding medical terminology.

这些医疗保健项目还汇集了来自圣玛丽医院、多伦多病童医院 (HSC)、圣托马斯医院和威尔士大学的众多软件和医疗保健专业人员。多伦多病童医院的护士安妮·凯西和分析师哈齐姆·蒂米米协助完成了最终的 Cosmos 模型。格里·戈尔德负责这项工作的筹备和推进。

The health care projects also involved many software and health care professionals from St. Mary's, the Hospital for Sick Children (HSC), St. Thomas's Hospital, and the University of Wales. Anne Casey, a nurse at HSC, and Hazim Timimi, an analyst, helped put together the final Cosmos model. Gerry Gold set up this work and made sure it kept going.

Brad Kain 对我关于再利用和组件的思考产生了很大的影响，他还承担了向我展示波士顿夜生活的重要任务。

Brad Kain has had a great impact on my thinking on reuse and components, as well as undertaking the important task of showing me the nightlife of Boston.

第四章中将医疗保健模型应用于公司财务的经历，对我而言，充分证明了分析模式在不同领域的实用性。Lynne Halpin 和 Craig Lockwood 领导了施乐公司的 MBFW 团队，而 Vivek Salgar 则将我们的概念性想法转化为 C++ 的残酷现实。

Applying the health care models to corporate finance in Chapter 4 was the experience that, for me, proved the usefulness of analysis patterns across different domains. Lynne Halpin and Craig Lockwood led the MBFW team at Xerox, and Vivek Salgar got our conceptual ideas into the brutal reality of C++.

大卫·克雷格、史蒂夫·谢泼德和他们在花旗银行的团队与我合作开发了模型，我从中汲取了第 9 章至第 11 章的金融模式。他们还从医疗保健领域进一步发展了第 12 章的许多架构理念，并教会了我很多关于伦敦金融城快节奏生活的知识。

David Creager, Steve Shepherd, and their team at Citibank worked with me in developing the models from which I drew the financial patterns in Chapters 9-11. They also further developed many of the architectural ideas of Chapter 12 from their health care origins, and taught me much about the frenetic life in The City.

弗雷德·皮尔负责我在花旗银行的工作安排和维护，当然，他开车时也经常吓到我。瓦尔贝克公司的丹尼尔·潘和哈齐姆·蒂米米则把我的许多模糊想法变成了详细的技术规范。

Fred Peel set up and maintained my work at Citibank, when not scaring me with his driving. Daniel Poon and Hazim Timimi from Valbecc got many of my fuzzy ideas into detailed specifications.

第六章的会计模式酝酿已久。Tom Daly、Peter Swettenham、Tom Hadfield 和他们各自的团队开发了模型，这些模型孕育了本书中的模式。Rich Garzaniti 帮我理清了会计术语。Kent Beck 则极大地改进了我的 Smalltalk 代码。

The accounting patterns in Chapter 6 have had a long gestation. Tom Daly, Peter Swettenham, Tom Hadfield, and their respective teams developed models that gave birth to the patterns in this book. Rich Garzaniti got my accounting terminology sorted out. Kent Beck did much to improve my Smalltalk.

第十四章是在詹姆斯·奥德尔的帮助下撰写的。

Chapter 14 was written with the help of James Odell.

我加入图案设计社群的时间比较晚，直到本书大部分内容完成后才开始深入了解这个社群。这是一个非常开放友好的群体，他们给予了我很多鼓励。肯特·贝克、沃德·坎宁安和吉姆·科普林鼓励我积极参与社群活动，并将我的想法发展成图案。拉尔夫·约翰逊对本书初稿提出了特别有益的意见。

I have been very much a latecomer to the patterns community, getting to know it well only after most of this book was written. It is a very open and friendly group that has done much to encourage my work. Kent Beck, Ward Cunningham, and Jim Coplein encouraged me to get involved with the community and to develop my ideas as patterns. Ralph Johnson provided particularly helpful comments on the first draft of this book.

我收到了许多审稿人的宝贵意见，在此我想提及他们的名字：Dave Collins、Ward Cunningham（Cunningham & Cunningham, Inc.）、Henry A. Etlinger（罗切斯特理工学院计算机科学系）、Donald G. 第一章 引言

Chapter 1. Introduction

1.1 概念模型

1.1 Conceptual Models

大多数关于对象建模的书籍都会讨论分析和设计。但对于这两者之间的界限，却鲜有共识。对象开发的一个重要原则是，软件的结构要能够反映问题的结构。这一原则的一个结果是，分析和设计生成的模型最终往往非常相似，这使得许多人误以为两者之间没有区别。

Most books on object modeling talk about analysis and design. There is little agreement on where the boundary between these two activities lies. An important principle in object development is designing software so that its structure reflects that of the problem. One result of this principle is that the models produced from both analysis and design end up deliberately similar, leading many people to think that there is no difference.

我认为分析和设计之间仍然存在区别，但这种区别正日益演变为侧重点的差异。进行分析时，你试图理解问题。在我看来，这不仅仅是列出用例中的需求[8]。用例是系统开发中非常重要甚至必不可少的一部分，但收集用例并非分析的终点。分析还包括深入探究表面需求，从而构建出问题本质的思维模型。

I believe a difference between analysis and design still exists, but it is increasingly becoming one of emphasis. When doing analysis you are trying to understand the problem. To my mind this is not just listing requirements in use-cases [8]. Use-cases are a valuable, if not essential, part of system development, but capturing them is not the end of analysis. Analysis also involves looking behind the surface requirements to come up with a mental model of what is going on in the problem.

假设有人想编写一个模拟斯诺克比赛的软件。这个问题可以从描述表面特征的使用场景来评估：“球员击打白球，使其以特定速度运动；白球以特定角度击中红球；红球沿特定方向运动一段距离。”你可以拍摄数百个这样的场景，并测量球速、角度和运动距离。但仅凭这些例子可能不足以编写一个好的模拟程序。要做好这项工作，你需要深入了解运动的本质，理解质量、速度、动量等相关的运动定律。理解这些定律将使软件的构建变得更加容易。

Consider someone who wants to write software to simulate a game of snooker. This problem could be evaluated in terms of use-cases that describe the surface features: "The player hits the white ball so it travels at a certain speed; it hits the red ball at a certain angle, and the red ball travels a certain distance and direction." You could film several hundred such incidents and measure ball speeds, angles, distances traveled. But these examples alone would probably not be enough to write a good simulation. To do the job well, you would need to look behind the surface to understand the laws of motion that relate mass, velocity, momentum, and the like. Understanding those laws would make it much easier to see how the software could be built.

斯诺克球问题的特殊之处在于，其规律众所周知，而且由来已久。在许多企业中，类似的原理却鲜为人知，我们需要努力去发掘它们。为此，我们需要构建一个概念模型——一个能够帮助我们理解和简化问题的思维模型。某种形式的概念模型是软件开发中必不可少的一部分，即使是最不加节制的黑客也会这样做。区别在于，我们是将概念建模视为一个独立的过程，还是将其视为整个软件设计过程的一个方面。

The snooker ball problem is unusual because the laws are well known and have been well known for a long time. In many enterprises the equiva lent foundations are not so well understood, and we have to make the effort to uncover them. To do this we create a conceptual model—a mental model that allows us to understand and simplify the problem. Some kind of conceptual model is a necessary part of software development, and even the most uncontrolled hacker does it. The difference is whether we think about conceptual modeling as a process in itself or as one aspect of the entire software design process.

重要的是要记住，概念模型是人为的产物。开发者用来创建类似斯诺克模拟程序的运动定律并非真实世界的一部分；它们代表的是一个由人类创造的真实世界模型。从工程学的角度来看，这些模型之所以有效，是因为它们能帮助我们更好地理解现实世界中发生的事情。此外，开发者可以使用多个模型；例如，对于斯诺克模拟，可以使用牛顿模型或爱因斯坦模型。有人可能会认为爱因斯坦模型更准确，因为它考虑了球速变化引起的质量变化，因此更加精确。然而，开发者几乎肯定会更倾向于牛顿模型，因为球速非常低，对模拟结果的影响微乎其微，但却会增加很多额外的复杂性。这说明了一个重要的原则：没有绝对正确或错误的模型，只有最适合当前任务的模型。

It is important to remember that a conceptual model is a human artifact. The laws of motion that a developer uses to create something like the snooker simulation are not part of the real world; they represent a model of the real world, a model created by human beings. They are effective, in engineering terms, because they allow us to better understand what happens in the real world. Also, a developer can use more than one model; for the snooker simulation a Newtonian or Einsteinian model could be used. You could argue that the Einsteinian model would be more correct because it takes into account changes of mass due to the speed the balls are traveling and is thus more precise. The developer would almost certainly prefer the Newtonian model, however, because the speeds would be so low that they would make a negligible difference to the simulation but would involve a lot of extra complexity. This illustrates an important principle: There is no right or wrong model, merely one that is more useful for the job at hand.

建模原理
Modeling Principle
模型本身没有对错之分，只有实用性高低之分。
Models are not right or wrong; they are more or less useful.

模型的选择会影响最终系统的灵活性和可重用性。你可能会认为开发者应该使用爱因斯坦模型，因为这样生成的软件足够灵活，可以处理涉及原子碰撞的问题。但这其实是一条危险的道路。在系统中构建过多的灵活性会导致其过于复杂，这是一种糟糕的工程设计。工程设计需要在构建和维护产品的成本与其提供的功能之间进行权衡。要构建符合特定用途的软件，你必须开发一个符合自身需求的理论模型。你需要尽可能简化的模型。不要添加你不太可能用到的灵活性。

The choice of model affects the flexibility and reusability of the resulting system. You might argue that the developer should use an Einsteinian model because the resulting software would be flexible enough to handle problems involving atomic collisions. But this is a dangerous path to go down. Building too much flexibility into a system can make it too complex, and this is bad engineering. Engineering demands a trade-off between the cost of building and maintaining an artifact and the features it will provide. To build software that is fit for a purpose, you have to develop a conceptual model that is appropriate to your needs. You need the simplest model you can get away with. Don't add flexibility you are unlikely to use.

最简单的模型未必是你首先想到的。找到一个简单的解决方案需要花费大量的时间和精力，这可能会令人沮丧。人们常常会对一个简单的模型说“哦，是啊，这显而易见”，然后心想“那为什么花了这么长时间才想到呢？” 但简单的模型总是值得付出努力的。它们不仅让开发更容易，更重要的是，它们让未来的维护和扩展更加便捷。这就是为什么用更简单但同样有效的软件来替换现有的软件是值得的。

The simplest model is not necessarily the first one you think of. Finding a simple solution takes a lot of time and effort, which can be frustrating. People often react to a simple model by saying "Oh yes, that's obvious" and thinking "So why did it take so long to come up with it?" But simple models are always worth the effort. Not only do they make things easier to build, but more importantly they make them easier to maintain and extend in the future. That's why it is worth replacing software that works with simpler software that also works.

如何表达概念模型？对许多人来说，概念模型是内置于他们使用的软件语言中的。语言的优势在于，你可以执行模型来验证其正确性并进行更深入的探索。这可不是什么小优势；我经常在概念建模中使用 Smalltalk。另一个优势是，你最终必须将模型转换为编程语言，因此使用目标语言进行建模可以省去转换步骤。（有一些工具可以解释或编译分析和设计模型，从而减少与转换相关的问题。）

How do you express a conceptual model? For many people the conceptual model is built into their software language. The advantage of a language is that you can execute a model to verify its correctness and to further explore it. This is no small advantage; I often use Smalltalk in my conceptual modeling. Another advantage is that you have to turn the model into a programming language eventually, so modeling in your target language saves the step of translation. (There are tools that can interpret or compile analysis and design models, thus reducing the problems associated with translation.)

使用某种编程语言的风险在于，很容易陷入使用该语言的各种细节中，而忽略了你试图理解的问题本身。（对于像 Smalltalk 这样的高级语言来说，这个问题不太明显。我认识几位才华横溢的概念建模师，他们就用这种语言进行建模。）用编程语言建模的另一个风险是，模型可能会被绑定到该语言上。模型可能会用到其他语言所不具备的特性。这并不意味着概念模型不能移植到另一种语言，但移植过程会更加困难。

The danger of using a language is that it is easy to get lost in the issues of using that language and lose sight of the problem you are trying to understand. (This is less of a problem with higher-level languages, such as Smalltalk. I know several gifted conceptual modelers who do their modeling in that language.) Modeling in a programming language also presents the danger of tying the models to that language. The model may use features of that language that are not available in other languages. This does not mean that the conceptual model cannot be moved to another language, but it can make the process more difficult.

为了避免这些问题，许多人使用分析和设计技术进行概念建模。这些技术可以帮助人们专注于概念问题而非软件设计问题，而且更容易教授给领域专家。分析和设计技术利用图形来增强表达效果。它们可能很严谨，但并非必须如此。旨在实现可执行性的技术必须严谨，但当分析方法与编程语言结合使用时，则无需如此严谨。

To avoid these problems, many people use analysis and design techniques for conceptual modeling. These techniques can help people concen trate on conceptual rather than software design issues, and they can be easier to teach to domain experts. Analysis and design techniques use graphics to be more expressive. They may be rigorous, but they don't have to be. Techniques designed to be executable must be rigorous, but when analysis methods are used in conjunction with a programming language, they need not be as rigorous.

我使用分析和设计技术的主要原因之一是让领域专家参与其中。让领域专家参与概念建模至关重要。我相信，只有真正了解该领域的人员——该领域的全职工作者，而不是软件开发人员，无论他们在该领域工作了多久——才能构建有效的模型。如果要让领域专家进行概念建模，就必须对他们进行培训。我曾向客户服务主管、医生、护士、金融交易员和企业财务分析师教授面向对象分析和设计技术。我发现，IT背景对建模技能既无帮助也无阻碍。我认识的最优秀的建模师是一位伦敦医院的医生。作为专业的分析师和建模师，我为这个过程带来了宝贵的技能：我能够提供严谨性，我知道如何运用这些技术，而且我的局外人视角可以挑战既有的观点。然而，所有这些都还不够。无论我在医疗保健计算领域做了多少工作，我永远无法像医生或护士那样了解医疗保健。专家知识是构建良好分析模型的核心。

One of the main reasons I use analysis and design techniques is to involve domain experts. It is essential to have domain experts involved in conceptual modeling. I believe that effective models can only be built by those that really understand the domain—full-time workers in the domain, not software developers, no matter how long they have worked in the domain. If domain experts are to do conceptual modeling, they must be taught. I have taught OO analysis and design techniques to customer service supervisors, doctors, nurses, financial traders, and corporate financial analysts. I have found that an IT background is neither a help nor a hindrance to skill in modeling. The best modeler I know is a physician at a London hospital. As the professional analyst and modeler, I bring valuable skills to the process: I can provide rigor, I know how to use the techniques, and my outsider's view can challenge accepted wisdom. All this is not enough. However much work I do in health care computing, I will never know? as much about health care as a doctor or nurse. Expert knowledge is central to a good analysis model.

分析技术旨在独立于软件技术。理想情况下，概念建模技术应该像运动定律一样完全独立于软件技术。这种独立性可以防止技术阻碍对问题的理解，并且最终得到的模型对所有类型的软件技术都同样适用。然而，在实践中，这种纯粹性并不存在。我尝试开发完全专注于问题的概念模型，但我的技术是面向对象的，因此体现了一种软件设计方法。通过将本书中的模型与 David Hay [7] 的模型进行比较，您可以很好地了解软件技术如何影响概念建模。我们都在尝试构建概念模型，但由于他使用关系型技术而我使用面向对象技术，因此我们的结果不同。这是软件本质的必然结果。构建软件就是构建虚拟机。我们用来构建软件的语言既可以控制物理机器，也可以表达问题的需求。我们语言发生变化的原因之一是我们找到了表达问题需求的更好方法。因此，这些语言的变化会影响我们构建概念模型的方式。尽管存在一些棘手的领域（参见第 14 章），但将所得模型转换为面向对象的软件并不难。

Analysis techniques are intended to be independent of software technology. Ideally a conceptual modeling technique is totally independent of software technology, as are the laws of motion. This independence would prevent technology from hindering an understanding of the problem, and the resulting model would be equally useful for all kinds of software technology. In practice this purity does not occur. I try to develop very conceptual models that focus entirely on the problem, yet my techniques are object-oriented and hence reflect a software design approach. You can get a good sense of how software technology affects conceptual modeling by comparing the models in this book with those of David Hay [7]. We are both trying to build conceptual models, yet our results are different because he uses a relational technique and I use an object-oriented one. This is an inevitable result of the nature of software. Building software is building virtual machines. The languages in which we build software can both control the physical machine and express the needs of the problem. One of the reasons our languages change is because we find better ways to express the needs of a problem. These language changes thus influence the way we build conceptual models. Despite a few tricky areas (see Chapter 14), the resulting models are not difficult to turn into object-oriented software.

不过，我现在需要提醒一点，概念模型与软件接口密切相关，而非软件实现。面向对象软件的一个重要特点是它将接口与实现分离。遗憾的是，这种区分在实践中很容易被忽略，因为常用语言并没有明确区分这两者。软件组件的接口（类型）和实现（类）之间的区别至关重要。“四人帮”著作[6]中的许多重要的基于委托的模式都依赖于这种区分。在实现这些模型时，切勿忘记这种区别。

One caution I do need to raise now, however, is that conceptual models relate closely to software interfaces rather than software implementations. One of the important things about object-oriented software is that it separates interface from implementation. Unfortunately this distinction is too easily lost in practice because common languages do not make an explicit distinction between the two. The difference between a software component's interface (its type) and its implementation (its class) is extremely important. Many important delegation-based patterns in the "Gang of Four" book [6] rely on this distinction. When implementing these models, don't forget the difference.

建模原理
Modeling Principle
概念模型与接口（类型）相关联，而不是与实现（类）相关联。
Conceptual models are linked to interfaces (types) not implementations (classes).

1.2 图案的世界

1.2 The World of Patterns

近几年来，模式已成为对象设计社区最热门的话题之一。它们正迅速成为前沿潮流，引发了广泛的关注和炒作。我们也看到社区内部就模式的定义展开了激烈的争论，其中不乏关于模式究竟是什么的争论。显然，要找到一个普遍认可的模式定义并非易事。

In the last couple of years, patterns have become one of the hottest topics in the object community. They are rapidly becoming the leading-edge fad, generating a huge amount of interest and the usual hype. We are also seeing internal battles over what fits into the community, including many arguments about exactly what a pattern is. Certainly it is difficult to find any common definition of pattern.

模式运动的根源来自多个方面。近年来，越来越多的人认为软件界在描述和推广优秀设计实践方面做得不够好。方法论层出不穷，但它们定义的只是描述设计的语言，而不是描述实际的设计。过去（现在依然如此）缺乏基于实践描述实用设计的技术论文，而这些论文本可以用来进行教育和启发。正如拉尔夫·约翰逊和沃德·坎宁安所说：“即使拥有最新的技术，项目失败的原因仍然是缺乏常规的解决方案”[4]

The roots of the patterns movement come from various sources. In recent years an increasing number of people felt that the software world was not very good at describing and proliferating good design practice. Methodologies abounded, but they defined a language for describing designs rather than describing actual designs. There was (and still is) a dearth of technical papers describing useful designs based on practice, which could be used to educate and inspire. As Ralph Johnson and Ward Cunningham put it: "Projects fail despite the latest technology for lack of ordinary solutions" [4],

模式的形成源于多项举措。Smalltalk 的两位先驱 Kent Beck 和 Ward Cunningham 接触到了 Christopher Alexander 的思想，后者发展了一套架构理论和模式集合。20 世纪 90 年代初，Bruce Anderson 在 OOPSLA 大会上主持了研讨会，探讨如何编写一本软件架构师手册。Jim Coplien 的 C++ 著作 [3] 描述了 C++ 中常用的惯用法。这些人中的一些人组建了 Hillside Group，以进一步探索这些理念。

Patterns evolved from several initiatives. Kent Beck and Ward Cunning-ham, two of the pioneers of Smalltalk, came across the ideas of Christopher Alexander, who had developed a theory and collection of patterns in architecture. Bruce Anderson led workshops at OOPSLA in the early 1990s that investigated building a handbook for software architects. Jim Coplien's C++ book [3] described idioms useful in C++. A number of these people formed the Hillside Group to explore these ideas further.

1994 年，希尔赛德小组创办了具有开创性的《四人帮》一书 [6] 和 PLoP（编程模式语言）会议 [4]，这引发了公众对这一运动的更大了解。

A greater public knowledge of the movement was triggered by the publication of the seminal "Gang of Four" book [6] and the PLoP (Pattern Language of Programming) conference started by the Hillside group in 1994 [4].

我之前与这个日益壮大的社群接触甚少。我一直很想读一些描述概念模型的书籍，因为我觉得这类书籍能给我带来很多灵感。但我总觉得，在积累到足够多的模型，足以写出一本有价值的书之前，我无法着手撰写这类文章。我对模式运动很感兴趣，也觉得他们的许多原则都很有吸引力，但我却被一种印象所打消：这个群体似乎是一个封闭的小圈子，痴迷于建筑师克里斯托弗·亚历山大，而且他们的模式写作风格非常程式化。去年，我与他们有了更多接触，并参加了第二届PLoP会议。模式社群最显著的特点是其成员构成非常多元化。的确，有些人似乎把亚历山大的著作奉为圭臬，并乐于就不同的解读展开辩论。当然，也有很多人认为亚历山大的理论已经过时。有些人似乎在模式中看到了某种神秘的力量，而有些人则无法忍受模式中那种“感性”的表达方式。有些人认为模式颠覆了分析和设计方法，有些人认为概念建模是浪费时间，还有些人鼓励我写这本书，以展示分析或概念模式是什么样的。

I had had very little contact with this growing community. I had long wanted to read books that described conceptual models, because I felt such books would give me good ideas. I didn't feel I could write about such things until I had enough models to form a worthwhile book. I was interested in the patterns movement and I found many of their principles appealing, but I was put off by the impression of a cliquey group that was obsessed with the architect Christopher Alexander and had a very stylized form of pattern writing. In the last year I have had more contact and attended the second PLoP. The most noticeable aspect of the patterns community is that it is quite a diverse group. Yes, there are those who seem to regard Alexander's works as sacred text, with alternative interpretations to be argued over. There are also plenty of those who dismiss Alexander as irrelevant. There are those who seem to see a mystical virtue in patterns, and those who can't stand the "touchy-feely" aspect of patterns. There are those who see patterns as overturning analysis and design methods, those who see conceptual modeling as a waste of time, and those who have encouraged me to produce this book to show what analysis, or conceptual, patterns can be like.

软件模式的概念并非面向对象社区所独有；David Hay 就数据模型模式撰写了一本极具价值的著作[7]。这些模型遵循关系数据建模风格，但它们是非常概念化的模型。即使您使用的是面向对象技术，这些模型仍然很有价值。

The idea of software patterns is not confined to the object-oriented community; David Hay has written a valuable book on data model patterns [7]. The models follow relational data modeling style, but they are very conceptual models. This makes the models valuable even if you are using object technology.

1.2.1 克里斯托弗·亚历山大

1.2.1 Christopher Alexander

对许多人来说，“模式”一词在软件领域的出现几乎完全归功于加州大学伯克利分校建筑学教授克里斯托弗·亚历山大（Christopher Alexander）的工作。亚历山大发展了一系列关于建筑模式的理论，并将其发表在一系列著作中。他的《模式语言》[1]——一本建筑模式目录——被视为软件模式书籍的雏形。许多模式编写者在一定程度上借鉴了他的模式编写风格。他提出的“一种无法命名的特质”这一概念经常被引用，并被视为所有优秀模式应具备的属性。

For many people, the word pattern has appeared in software almost entirely due to the work of Christopher Alexander, a professor of architecture at the University of California at Berkeley. Alexander developed a range of theories about patterns in architecture and published these in a series of books. His pattern language book [1], a catalog of patterns in architecture, is seen as the prototype to patterns books in software. His style of writing patterns is used, to some extent, by many pattern writers. His phrase "a quality without a name" is often quoted as an attribute that all good patterns should have.

然而，许多人否认亚历山大在软件模式领域的核心地位。彼得·戈德指出，许多其他领域的作者也运用了模式的概念，他认为其中许多人比亚历山大更胜一筹。许多人质疑亚历山大在建筑界的地位：他的思想远未被普遍接受。“四人帮”的著作对软件模式的影响远超亚历山大的作品，而这四位作者中有三位在撰写该书之前甚至没有读过亚历山大的著作。

Many people, however, would deny Alexander his central role as the inspiration for software patterns. Peter Goad points out that the notion of patterns is used by many writers in other fields, many of whom he thinks are better examples than Alexander. Many people question Alexander's standing in the architectural profession: His ideas are by no means universally accepted. The "Gang of Four" book has had much more influence in software patterns than Alexander's work, and three out of those four authors had not read Alexander before writing that book.

1.2.2 文学形式

1.2.2 The Literary Form

模式写作最显著的特点之一是其写作形式。模式通常以非常固定的格式编写。然而，模式并没有唯一的格式，只需快速浏览一下PLoP论文即可证实这一点。许多人效仿亚历山大的风格，也有人遵循“四人帮”的格式。

One of the most distinctive features of pattern writing is the form in which it is often done. Frequently patterns are written in a very set format. There is, however, no single format, as a quick glance through PLoP papers will confirm. Many people follow the inspiration of Alexander's style. Others follow the format used by the "Gang of Four."

人们通常认为，无论以何种形式编写，模式都包含四个基本部分：模式适用的背景、模式所解决的问题、影响解决方案形成的因素，以及解决这些因素的解决方案。这种形式既可以带有特定标题，也可以不带标题，但它是许多已发表模式的基础。这种形式之所以重要，是因为它支持将模式定义为“针对特定背景问题的解决方案”，这一定义将模式的边界限定于单一的问题-解决方案对。

It is commonly said that a pattern, however it is written, has four essential parts: a statement of the context where the pattern is useful, the problem that the pattern addresses, the forces that play in forming a solution, and the solution that resolves those forces. This form appears with and without specific headings but underlies many published patterns. It is an important form because it supports the definition of a pattern as "a solution to a problem in context," a definition that fixes the bounds of the pattern to a single problem-solution pair.

对许多人来说，使用固定的格式，无论是“四人帮”格式还是“背景-问题-原因-解决方案”格式，都是判断文章模式是否具有代表性的因素之一。使用公认的模式格式，能够清晰地表明该文章模式与普通技术写作有所不同。

To many people the use of a fixed format, whether that of the "Gang of Four" or the context-problem-forces-solution form, is one determiner of a pattern. Use of an accepted pattern form clearly marks the pattern as something different from the average piece of technical writing.

然而，固定的形式也有其自身的缺点。例如，在本书中，我并不认为问题-解决方案对总是构成模式的理想单元。本书中的几个模式展示了同一个问题如何根据不同的权衡取舍，以多种方式解决。虽然这完全可以针对每种解决方案分别构建模式，但将几种解决方案放在一起讨论的做法在我看来并不逊色于模式实践。当然，模式形式的内容本身很有道理——任何技术写作通常都包含背景、问题、影响因素和解决方案。但这是否意味着每篇技术写作都可以算作一种模式，则是另一个值得探讨的问题。

A fixed form carries its own disadvantages, however. In this book, for instance, I do not find that a problem-solution pair always makes a good unit for a pattern. Several patterns in this book show how a single problem can be solved in more than one way, depending on various trade-offs. Although this could always be expressed as separate patterns for each solution, the notion of discussing several solutions together strikes me as no less elegant than pattern practice. Of course, the contents of the pattern forms make a lot of sense—any technical writing usually includes context, problem, forces, and solution. Whether this makes every piece of technical writing a pattern is another matter for discussion.

我完全赞同模式形式的一个原则，那就是它们应该被命名。模式的优势之一在于它能够丰富开发词汇。只需说“这里使用保护代理”或“我们使用观察来记录产品指标”，我们就能非常有效地传达我们的设计理念。当然，模式本身并没有什么独特之处；为概念创造新术语是技术写作中常用的技巧，但寻找模式本身就能促进这一过程。

One principle of pattern form that I do agree with unreservedly is that they should be named. One advantage of patterns work is how it can enrich the vocabulary of development. By just saying "use a protection proxy here" or "we used observations to record product metrics," we can communicate our design ideas very effectively. Again, there is nothing unique about patterns here; it is a common technique of technical writing to coin new terms for concepts, but looking for patterns encourages this process.

1.2.3 作者的抽象程度

1.2.3 The Author's Level of Abstraction

对许多模式研究者来说，模式的关键要素之一在于，它们是通过观察日常开发过程中发生的事情而发现的，而非学术臆造。我认为这一点尤为重要。本书中的所有模式都源于一个或多个实际项目，并描述了这些项目中的实用要点。

To many patterns people, one of the key elements of patterns is that they are discovered by looking at what happens in day-to-day development, rather than by academic invention. This is an element that I find particularly important. All the patterns in this book are the result of one or more actual projects and describe useful highlights in that work.

我选择了一些我认为对其他开发者有用的模式收录到本书中。这些模式不仅适用于同一领域的开发者，而且通常在其他领域也同样适用。投资组合模式（参见 9.2 节）就是一个很好的例子。该模式最初是为了将金融合约分组而创建的。通过定义一个隐式查询，该模式可以用来对任何类型的对象进行分组，并且其抽象程度足以使其适用于任何领域。我亲眼见证了这一点：在本书初稿完成后，我们在另一个与交易完全无关的项目中多次使用了该模式。

I chose patterns to include in this book that I believe are useful to other developers. These patterns are not only useful to developers within the same domain as the pattern, but frequently a pattern is useful in other domains as well. A good example of this is the portfolio pattern (see Section 9.2). This pattern was originally created as a way of grouping financial contracts together. This pattern can be used to group any kind of object by defining an implicit query and is sufficiently abstract to be used in any domain. I've seen evidence of this: After the early drafts of this book were written, we used this pattern in several places in another project, completely independent of trading.

我面临的问题是，我应该如何看待这种广泛的抽象？如果我遇到一个我认为可以在更多领域发挥作用的模式，那么我应该如何抽象这个模式？将其抽象到超出其原始领域的问题在于，我无法确定其有效性。该模式出现的项目经过了长时间的讨论、实施，以及（最重要的是）领域专家的知识验证。一旦我进一步抽象，我就离开了这些安全的港湾，只能猜测我的发现会在茫茫大海中如何生存。未知领域太多。因此，我的观点（似乎很多模式开发者都认同）是，你必须判断该模式是否对你所在的领域有用，因为你比我更了解你的领域，或者你是否能够接触到相关的领域专家。在本书中，我使用示例来说明模式的更广泛适用性。任何超出模式原始领域的示例都只是初步的，但它们旨在激发你的想象力，让你扪心自问：“这对我有用吗？”

The question before me is how much should I make of this wide abstraction. If I come across a pattern that I think could be useful in more domains than the one I found it in, how abstract should I make that pattern? The problem with abstracting it beyond its original domain is that I cannot be as certain of its validity. The project that the pattern appeared in tested the pattern through long debate, implementation, and (above all) the knowledge of the domain experts. As soon as I abstract further, I leave those safe harbors behind and guess how my discovery might fare on the open sea. There are many unknowns out there. Thus my view (which many patterns people seem to share) is that you must judge whether the pattern is useful to your domain, which you know infinitely better than I do, or you have access to the appropriate domain experts. In this book I use examples to suggest the wider applicability of a pattern. Any example that lies out of the original domain of the pattern is tentative, but they are there to spark your imagination, to make you ask yourself, "Is this useful for me?"

1.3 本书中的模式

1.3 The Patterns in this Book

我用来定义“模式”的术语是指在某个实际情境中已被证明有效，并且可能在其他情境中也同样有效的理念。我使用“理念”一词是为了强调模式可以是任何事物。它可以是一组协作对象，例如“四人帮”的模式，或者Coplien的项目组织原则[5]。“实际情境”这一表述反映了模式源于真实项目的实践经验这一事实。人们常说模式是被发现的，而不是被发明的。这在某种意义上是正确的，因为只有当人们意识到模型可能具有普遍的用途时，它们才会转化为模式。特定的项目先于模式出现，并非特定项目中的所有想法都是模式；模式是开发者认为在其他情境中可能有用的东西。理想情况下，这种想法来源于在其他地方的实际应用，但也可能仅仅反映了原始开发者的观点。本书中的模式分为两类：

The definition I use for pattern is an idea that has been useful in one practical context and will probably be useful in others. I use the term idea to bring out the fact that a pattern can be anything. It can be a group of collaborating objects, as in the "Gang of Four's" patterns, or Coplien's principles for project organization [5]. The phrase practical context reflects the fact that patterns are developed out of the practical experience of a real project. It is often said that patterns are discovered rather than invented. This is true in the sense that models turn into patterns only when it is realized that they may have a common usefulness. A particular project comes first, and not all ideas of a particular project are patterns; patterns are those things that developers think may be useful in other contexts. Ideally this comes from actually using them elsewhere, but it may just reflect the opinion of the original developers. The patterns in this book fall into two categories:

分析模式是一组概念，代表业务建模中的通用结构。它可能仅适用于一个领域，也可能跨越多个领域。分析模式是本书的核心内容。

• Analysis patterns are groups of concepts that represent a common construction in business modeling. It may be relevant to only one domain, or it may span many domains. Analysis patterns form the heart of this book.

• 辅助模式本身也是一种模式，具有很高的价值。然而，它们在本书中扮演着特殊的角色：它们阐述了如何运用分析模式，使其真正落地。

• Supporting patterns are patterns in themselves and are valuable on their own. They have a special role in this book, however: They describe how to take the analysis patterns and apply them, to make them real.

1.3.1 建模示例

1.3.1 Examples for Modeling

一般而言，分析与设计方面的书籍都是入门读物，通常侧重于解释作者的方法论。这类入门书籍往往忽略了建模中许多重要的问题——这些问题只有在大型项目的背景下才会显现。脱离实际项目环境，这些问题难以理解，需要读者具备一定的建模经验才能充分领会。

The average book on analysis and design is an introductory book that typically explains the author's methodology. Such introductory books do not cover many important problems in modeling—problems that can only surface in the context of a large project. Such problems are difficult to understand outside that context and require the reader to have some modeling experience to fully appreciate them.

模式为解决这些问题提供了一种很好的方法。本书中的许多模式通过分析某一特定领域中更容易理解的具体问题，来处理一般的建模问题。例如，处理可以链接到单个对象实例的方法（参见第 6.6 节）、状态图的子类型化（参见第 10.4 节）、将模型分为知识层和操作层（参见第 2.5 节）以及使用组合按查询对对象进行分组（参见第 9.2 节）。

Patterns provide a good way of looking at these problems. Many patterns in this book deal with general modeling issues by looking at a particular problem in one domain, where it is easier to understand. Examples are the handling of methods that can be linked to individual object instances (see Section 6.6), subtyping of state diagrams (see Section 10.4), separating models into knowledge and operational levels (see Section 2.5) and using portfolios to group objects by a query (see Section 9.2).

1.3.2 图案的起源

1.3.2 Origins of the Patterns

如上所述，本书中的模式基于我个人将对象建模应用于大型企业信息系统的经验。这也解释了为什么它们的选择在某种程度上是随机的。我只能撰写我了解的模式，也就是说，只能撰写来自我参与过的项目的模式。

As mentioned above, the patterns in this book are based on my personal experiences applying object modeling to large corporate information systems. This explains their somewhat random selection. I can only write about patterns I know about, that is, patterns that come from projects in which I have participated.

尽管这些模型基于耗时数月的密集项目，但我并未尝试讨论完整的模型。我可以写一整本书来描述一个领域。虽然这样的书对于该领域的从业者来说会很有趣（我也希望将来能有这样的书出版），但我希望这本书能够跨越多个领域，促进它们之间的交流与融合。第二个原因是，为了保护客户的隐私，我选择描述一些关键点而非完整的模型。

Although these models are based on intensive projects that sometimes took several months to complete, I have made no attempt to discuss full models. I could write a whole book describing one domain. While such a book would be interesting to someone working in that field (and I hope such books will appear one day), I wanted this book to span fields and cross-pollinate between them. A second reason for describing highlights rather than complete models is client confidentiality.

我并未完全忠实于原模型。我出于多种原因进行了修改。我简化了一些抽象概念，既保留了原模型的精神，又使其更易于解释和理解。我还对一些模型进行了略微超出特定领域的抽象。这些抽象仅限于项目中认为合理但超出项目范围的概念。在某些情况下，我修改了模型，使其反映我的想法，而非项目团队选择的模型。作为顾问，我只能提供建议，有时我的观点未必能被采纳。在这种情况下，我在文中呈现了双方的观点，但通常会以我自己的观点为基础进行阐述。

I have not attempted to be entirely faithful to the models. I have made changes for several reasons. I have simplified some of the abstractions, pre-serving the spirit of the original while making it easier to explain and to follow. I have also abstracted some models a little above the specific domain. The abstractions are limited to those that were considered reasonable in the project but fell outside the scope of the project. In some cases I have altered the models so that they reflect my ideas rather than those chosen by the project team. As a consultant, I can only advise, and sometimes my view does not win. In these cases I have presented both points of view in the text but tend to build on my own opinions.

在对象类型命名方面，我一直遵循与源项目命名一致的原则。虽然有很多次我都想更改名称，但正如任何建模师都知道的那样，命名可能是建模过程中最困难的部分之一。有些名称可能看起来有点奇怪，但没有哪个名称是完美的。

When it comes to the naming of object types, I have followed the principle of using the naming of the source project. There are many points where I have been tempted to change names, but as any modeler knows, naming can be one of the most difficult parts of modeling. Some of the names may seem a little odd, but no name is perfect.

1.3.3 跨领域模式

1.3.3 Patterns Across Domains

无论你从事哪个领域的工作，我都希望你能研究其他领域的模式。本书的大部分内容都包含通用的建模问题和经验教训，这些内容也适用于建模领域之外的其他领域。了解其他领域是进行抽象的宝贵工具。通常，需要具体的案例才能激发强大的抽象思维。许多专业人士不像我一样幸运，能够在多个不同领域工作。研究不同领域的模型往往能为看似无关的领域带来新的灵感。

Whatever domain you work in, I hope that you will study patterns outside your domain. Much of the book includes general modeling issues and lessons applicable outside the domain being modeled. Knowledge of other domains is a valuable tool for abstraction. Specific cases are usually necessary to trigger powerful abstractions. Many professionals do not share my luck in working in many different domains. Looking at models in different domains can often spring new ideas in an unrelated domain.

但研究其他领域的最大原因在于，不同领域之间的异同并非总是显而易见的。本书中最好的例证来自医疗保健领域，该领域在多个章节中都有详细阐述。在构建医疗保健模型之后，我参与了一个为一家大型制造企业提供财务分析支持的项目。该项目的核心问题在于理解高层财务指标的成因。事实证明，医疗保健模型（本质上是一个关于诊断和治疗的模型）非常适用（参见第3章和第4章）。

But the biggest reason for looking at other domains is that it is not always obvious when domains are the same or different. The best example of that in this book comes from the health care field, which is modeled in several chapters. After working on a health care model, I was involved in a project supporting financial analysis of a large manufacturing company. The problem revolved around understanding the causes of high-level financial indicators. The health care model, essentially a model about diagnosis and treatment, proved remarkably appropriate (see Chapters 3 and 4).

我怀疑存在少量高度通用的流程，它们跨越了系统开发和业务工程的传统界限。诊断和治疗模型就是其中之一；另一个是会计和库存模型（参见第六章）。许多不同的企业都可以使用一套非常相似的抽象流程模型。这引发了一些关于承诺的针对行业垂直类库开发的重要问题。我认为，真正的业务框架不会按照传统的业务线组织，而是按照抽象的概念流程组织。

I suspect that there are a small number of highly generic processes that cut across traditional boundaries of systems development and business engineering. The diagnosis and treatment model is one; another is the accounting and inventory model (see Chapter 6). Many diverse businesses can use a set of very similar abstract process models. This raises some significant questions about the promised development of vertical class libraries for industry sectors. I believe that true business frameworks will not be organized along traditional business lines but instead along abstract conceptual processes.

1.4 概念模型和业务流程重组

1.4 Conceptual Models and Business Process Reengineering

大多数读者会分析本书中的概念模型来辅助计算机系统的开发，但概念模型还有其他用途。优秀的系统分析师一直都明白，简单地将现有流程计算机化并非资源的有效利用。计算机只是让人们能够以不同的方式做事。然而，系统分析师发现很难将这些理念推广到足够深入的层面：他们的技术似乎仍然过于依赖软件思维。IT人员很难让业务领导者认真对待他们的想法。

Most readers will analyze the conceptual models in this book to help develop computer systems, but conceptual models have other purposes. Good systems analysts have always known that taking an existing process and simply computerizing it is not a good use of resources. Computers allow people to do things in a different way. Systems analysts have found it difficult to push these ideas far enough, however: Their techniques still seem too dependent on software thinking. IT people have a hard time getting business leaders to take their ideas seriously.

与吉姆·奥德尔[9]的合作一直让我专注于业务建模而非软件建模。约翰·爱德华兹（我早期的同事和灵感来源）一直称他的方法为流程工程，远早于业务流程重组（BPR）成为热门缩写词。运用面向对象技术进行概念建模，确实可以将系统分析和业务流程重组融为一体。我教过的所有领域专家都很快意识到这种方法的潜力，并以此为契机，以全新的视角思考他们各自的领域。只有领域专家才能真正运用这些理念。

Working with Jim Odell [9] has always immersed me in business modeling rather than software modeling. John Edwards (an early colleague and inspiration) always called his approach process engineering, long before BPR (business process reengineering) became a hot acronym. Using OO tech niques for conceptual modeling can really make systems analysis and BPR the same activity. All the domain experts that I have taught have quickly seized on its potential to think about their own field in a new way. Only the domain experts can really use and apply these ideas.

因此，本书中的模型对业务工程和软件工程同样适用。尽管业务工程的关注点大多在于流程，但这些模式大多是静态类型模型。这主要源于我所涉猎领域的经验。在医疗保健领域，我们发现，虽然可以构建适用于医疗保健各个环节的通用类型模型，但却难以构建许多有意义的通用动态模型。

The models in this book thus have as much to say about business engineering as they do about software engineering. Although much of the attention in business engineering is about process, most of these patterns are static type models. The basic reason for this is the experience from the domains I have worked with. In health care we found that although we could make generic type models, which applied to all parts of health care, we could not make many meaningful generic dynamic models.

类型模型非常重要。我喜欢把类型模型看作是定义业务语言的工具。这些模型提供了一种方法，可以提出许多有用的概念，而这些概念是流程建模的基础。事实证明，问责制的概念在医疗保健领域的保密政策建模中非常有用。在处理薪资管理工作中，我看到了建模如何改变了人们对流程的理解和认知。

The type models are important. I like to think of type models as defining the language of the business. These models thus provide a way of coming up with useful concepts that underlie a great deal of the process modeling. The concept of accountability has proven very useful in modeling confidentiality policies in health care. In working with payroll I have seen how modeling has changed the language and perception of the process.

1.5 模式和框架

1.5 Patterns and Frameworks

如果问普通专业人士面向对象技术的主要优势是什么，答案几乎总是“重用”。其愿景是让开发者能够利用经过实践检验的现成组件来组装系统。然而，这些愿景的实现进展缓慢。在某些情况下，重用开始显现，尤其是在图形用户界面（GUI）开发和数据库交互领域。但在业务层面，重用尚未得到充分体现。

If the average professional is asked what the principal benefit of object technology is, the answer is almost always reuse. The vision is that of developers being able to assemble systems from tried and tested off-the-shelf components. Many of these visions have been very slow to appear. In some cases reuse is beginning to show, most notably in GUI development and database interaction. Where they are not appearing is at the business level.

医疗保健、银行、制造业等领域没有相应的组件，因为这些领域没有标准框架。软件组件最成功的例子是 Visual Basic。其成功的关键在于所有组件都基于同一个框架——Visual Basic 环境。组件开发者可以预先了解产品将要运行的环境，从而进行开发。

There are no components for health care, banking, manufacturing, or the like because there is no standard framework for these areas. The most successful example of software components is that for Visual Basic. A vital part of this is because all the components are based on a common framework—the Visual Basic environment. Component developers can develop their wares knowing what kind of world they will live in.

为了实现信息系统组件的重用，必须建立一个通用框架。一个有效的框架不应过于复杂或臃肿，而应具有广泛的适用性，并基于该领域的有效概念模型。开发这样的框架在技术和政治层面都面临诸多挑战。

To accomplish component reuse for information systems, a common framework must be established. An effective framework must not be too complex or too bulky. It should be widely applicable across a large domain and be based on an effective conceptual model of that domain. Developing such frameworks is difficult, both technically and politically.

本书并非旨在为各行各业定义框架。¹ 本书旨在描述对同一情境进行建模的多种替代方法；而框架则侧重于选择特定的模型。我希望本书能够鼓励人们思考此类框架，并对其发展产生影响。

This book does not attempt to define frameworks for various industries.1 This book is about describing alternative ways of modeling a situation; frameworks are about choosing a particular model. I hope this book will encourage people to think about such frameworks and will influence their development.

1.6 模式的使用

1.6 Using the Patterns

模式是软件领域的一项新兴技术。我们仍在探索如何帮助人们学习模式并将其应用于实际工作中。本书收录了大量模式，很容易让人感到不知所措。

Patterns are a new development in software. We are still developing ways to help people learn about patterns and use them in their work. Faced with a large body of patterns in this book, it is easy to be overwhelmed.

首先要做的就是了解全书的整体脉络。读完本章导论后，我建议您阅读本书每一章的引言。章节引言能让您了解本章涵盖的主题。当然，您也可以按顺序阅读每一章，但我尽量让本书结构清晰，即使您不必阅读每一章也能有所收获。如果您专注于某个特定领域，可以先阅读几个您认为相关的章节。还有人建议先浏览图表。如果发现什么图表引起了您的兴趣，那就阅读相关的示例。这些示例通常都很有帮助。

The first thing to do is to get a general orientation. After reading this introductory chapter, I suggest reading the introduction to each chapter in the book. The chapter introduction gives you an idea of the topics covered in the chapter. Obviously you can then go ahead and read every chapter, but I have tried to write the book so that you don't have to read every chapter to get something out of it. If you are working in a particular area, you can read a couple of chapters that you think may be appropriate. Another approach people have suggested is to look at the diagrams. If something catches your eye as interesting, then read the examples. The examples are often a good

值得一提的是，本书的许多章节都基于一个专为医疗保健设计的概念框架——Cosmos 临床过程模型[2]。

It should be mentioned that many chapters are based on a conceptual framework designed for health care— the Cosmos Clinical Process Model [2].

这是一种帮助你判断该模式是否对你有用的方法。模式表也起到总结的作用，你可以从这里开始，也可以稍后用它来唤起记忆。

way of giving you an idea of whether the pattern will be useful to you. The Table of Patterns also acts as a summary, so you can start there or use it later to jog your memory.

一旦你发现了一个可能有用的模式，就去尝试一下。我发现，真正理解一个模式运作原理的唯一方法就是把它应用到我自己的问题上。你可以通过在纸上画出一个具体的模型，或者尝试编写一些代码来进行思考。尽量让模式适用，但不要用力过猛。你可能会发现这个模式并不合适。但这并没有浪费你的时间——你不仅了解了模式本身，可能也对问题有了更深的理解。如果一个模式不能完全满足你的需求，那就毫不犹豫地修改它。模式是建议，而不是规定。我把它们当作食谱书里的菜谱：它们为我提供了一个起点，一个制作菜肴的基本方案，我会根据自己的实际情况进行调整。无论模式多么适用，都要确保阅读模式的全文，以便了解它的局限性和重要特征。在使用模式之前和之后都要这样做。如果你发现了文中没有提到的模式知识，别光骂我——请发邮件告诉我（100031.3311@compuserve.com）。我很想了解大家是如何运用这些模式的。

Once you have identified a potentially useful pattern, then try it out. I've found that the only way I really understand how a pattern works is to try it out on a problem of my own. You can do this mentally by sketching a particular model on paper or by trying out some code. Try to make the pattern fit, but don't try too hard. You may find the pattern just wasn't the right one. You have not wasted your time—you have learned something about the pattern, and probably something about the problem, too. If a pattern does not fit your needs exactly, then don't hesitate to modify it. Patterns are suggestions, not prescriptions. I treat them as recipes in recipe books: They give me a starting point, a basic plan of putting the dish together, and I don't hesitate to adapt them to my particular circumstances. However well it fits, make sure you read the full text of the pattern so you get a sense of its limitations and important features. Do this both before you try to use it and after you have applied it. If you learn something about the pattern that isn't in the text, don't just curse me—send me an e-mail to let me know (100031.3311@compuserve .com). I am very interested to see how people use these patterns.

在项目中运用模式时，我必须考虑到客户的视角。有些客户不愿承认自己与其他客户相似，他们认为自己与众不同，并且对异类的想法抱有怀疑。对于这类客户，我不会直接透露模式。如果我发现某个模式可能适用，我会利用它来帮助我设计问题。这些问题或许能引导客户找到符合模式的答案，但我会采取间接的方式，通过提问来启发他们。

When I use patterns on a project, I have to be aware of the client's perspective. Some clients don't like to think of themselves as similar to any other client. They see themselves as very different and are suspicious of foreign ideas. With these clients I don't reveal the patterns. If I see where a pattern may apply, I use it to help me frame questions. These questions may well lead the client to something that fits the pattern, but I do it indirectly, using questions to prod them.

其他客户很高兴看到我公开使用各种模式，也乐于看到我重复使用以往的经验。对于这些客户，我会当着他们的面尝试这些模式，并仔细询问他们的感受，看看他们是否满意。重要的是要让他们明白，我并非将这些模式奉为圭臬，如果他们感到不舒服，我会尝试其他方法。这些客户的风险在于，他们可能会不加质疑地接受这些模式。

Other clients are happy to see me openly using patterns and are reassured to see that I am reusing my past work. With these clients I try the pattern out in front of them and question them closely to see if they are happy with it. It is important to be clear to them that I am not holding them up as gospel, and if they are not comfortable, I will try something else. The danger with these clients is that they might take the patterns without questioning them enough.

模式对于审视自己和他人的工作都至关重要。审视自己的工作时，要寻找是否存在类似的模式。如果发现，不妨尝试运用这些模式。即使你认为自己的方案更优，也要运用这些模式，并思考为什么你的方案更合适。我发现这是一种有助于更好地理解问题的有效方法。类似的流程也适用于审视他人的工作。如果你发现类似的模式，可以以此为切入点，向你正在审视的作品提出问题：与该模式相比，它的优势是什么？该模式是否提供了被审视模型所不具备的信息？如果有，这些信息是否重要？我会将我审视的模型与我已知的模式进行比较，通常我发现，当我问“为什么要这样做？”时，这个过程能让我更深入地了解问题和模式。仅仅通过询问“为什么”，就能学到很多东西，这真是令人惊叹。

Patterns are also important for reviews of both your own and others' work. For your own work, look to see if there are any patterns that are similar. If you find any, then try them out. Even if you believe your solution is better, use the patterns and work out why your solution is more appropriate. I find this a useful technique to understand problems better. A similar process works for reviewing the work of others. If you find a similar pattern, use it as a platform to ask questions of the work you are reviewing: What are its strengths compared to the pattern? Does the pattern give you anything the reviewed model does not have, and if so, is it important? I compare models I review with the patterns I know and usually find the process teaches me a great deal about both the problem and the patterns as I ask "Why do it this way?" It is amazing how much you learn by simply asking why.

写书总是意味着某种权威性。读者很容易把书当作确凿无疑的陈述。虽然有些作者可能对自己所说的话充满自信，但我并不这么认为。这些模式基于真实经验，因此我相信它们对您有价值。然而，我比任何人都更清楚地意识到它们的局限性。要真正具有权威性，这类模式必须经过大量的实践检验——这远远超出了我的经验范围。

Writing a book always implies a certain authority. It is easy for a reader to treat a book as a statement of certainty. Although some writers may have a sense of the certain correctness of what they say, I do not. These patterns are based on real experiences, and as such I am sure they will be of value to you. However, I am, more than anyone, painfully aware of their limitations. To be truly authoritative, patterns such as these must be tested by many applications—more than my experience allows.

这并不意味着这些模式毫无用处。它们凝聚了大量的思考。正如它们能帮助我快速入门建模工作一样，我也希望它们能对你有所帮助。重要的是要意识到，它们只是一个起点，而非终点。花时间理解这些模式的运作原理，同时也要探究它们的开发历程和局限性。不要害怕继续深入探索，提出更新更好的想法。当我与客户合作时，我不会把模式奉为圭臬，即使是我认为是自己创造的模式。每个项目的具体需求都会促使我去调整、完善和改进这些模式。

This does not mean that these patterns will not be helpful. They represent a lot of careful thought. Just as they give me a head start in my modeling work, I hope they will help you, too. The important thing is to be conscious that they are a starting point, not a destination. Spend time understanding how these patterns work, but look for how they were developed and the limitations they have. Don't be afraid to press on further and develop new and better ideas. When I work with a client, I do not take the patterns as gospel, even those I feel I invented. The demands of each project make me adapt, refine, and improve the patterns.

建模原理
Modeling Principle
模式只是起点，而不是终点。
Patterns are a starting point, not a destination.
建模原理
Modeling Principle
模型本身没有对错之分，只有实用性高低之分。
Models are not right or wrong, they are more or less useful.
