第八章 计划

Chapter 8. Planning

计划是任何大型项目的重要组成部分。许多管理者花费大量时间制定和跟踪计划。本章提供了一些基本的计划模式。这些模式既包括具体的计划，也包括可以重复使用的标准流程——即既定的规程，也包括规范的程序。

Planning is a vital part of any large endeavor. Many managers spend most of their time developing and tracking plans. This chapter provides some basic patterns for planning. The patterns describe individual plans as well as protocols—standard procedures that can be used repeatedly.

在某个领域内执行的任何操作都可以被记录。拟议操作和已执行操作（8.1）模式将操作的可能状态分为两个关键子类型，分别代表意图和实际发生的情况。类似地，操作的结束状态也被分为已完成操作和已放弃操作（8.2）。已放弃操作表示操作的最终取消，而暂时中止操作则用暂停（8.3）表示。

Any action carried out within a domain can be recorded. The proposed and implemented action (8.1) pattern divides the possible states of an action into two key subtypes, which represent the intention and what actually happens. The end of an action is similarly divided into completed and abandoned actions (8.2). An abandoned action represents a final cancellation of the action, and temporary holds on an action are represented by suspension (8.3).

计划（8.4）用于容纳一组拟定的行动。我们讨论计划的结构，这些结构记录了一组行动的依赖关系和顺序，同时允许单个行动出现在多个计划中。后一个特性对于协调多个计划至关重要，因为这些计划都是一次性的安排。协议（8.5）用于多次重复的标准计划。

A plan (8.4) is used to hold a group of proposed actions. We discuss structures of plans that record the dependency and sequencing of a group of actions while allowing a single action to appear in several plans. The latter property is essential to choreographing multiple plans, which are one -off arrangements. A protocol (8.5) is used for standard plans that are repeated many times.

执行一项行动需要资源。资源分配模式（8.6）描述了拟议行动和已执行行动的协议。我们考虑两种不同类型的资源：消耗品（由行动使用）和资产（随时间推移而使用）。

Carrying out an action requires resources. The resource allocation (8.6) pattern describes protocols for proposed and implemented actions. We consider two different kinds of resources: consumables, which are used by actions, and assets, which are used over time.

到目前为止，我们对计划的讨论主要集中在行动的规划和监控上，而忽略了行动的影响。我们讨论的最后一个模式处理结果函数和启动函数（8.7），它将本章中的模式与第三章中开发的观察和测量模式联系起来。这些函数使我们能够说明我们认为一项行动已经实现了什么（结果），一项方案应该实现什么（结果函数），以及什么条件促使我们启动一项方案（启动函数）。

So far our discussion of plans has focused on planning and monitoring actions and has ignored the effects of the actions. The final pattern we discuss handles outcome and start functions (8.7), which tie the patterns in this chapter with the observation and measurement patterns developed in Chapter 3. These functions allow us to say what we think an action has achieved (outcome), what a protocol should achieve (outcome function), and what conditions make us want to begin a protocol (start function).

规划是一个复杂的领域，本章中的模式，甚至比其他章节更甚，并非旨在涵盖所有情况。这些模式源自 Cosmos 临床流程模型 [1]，因此其构建方式明显倾向于支持医疗保健规划。资源方面的信息则来自与 Cosmos 的开发者和用户的未公开讨论，以及 NHS 通用基本规范 [2] 的影响。

Planning is a complex area, and the patterns in this chapter, even more than other chapters, are not intended to be complete. The patterns came out of the Cosmos Clinical Process Model [1], and its constructions are thus decidedly bent in directions that support health care planning. The resource side comes from unpublished discussions with the developers and users of Cosmos, and the influence of the NHS Common Basic Specification [2].

关键概念：拟议行动、已实施行动、计划、暂停、资源分配、资产、消耗品、临时资源、启动功能、结果功能

Key Concepts Proposed Action, Implemented Action, Plan, Suspension, Resource Allocation, Asset, Consumable, Temporal Resource, Start Function, Outcome Function

8.1 拟议和已实施的行动

8.1 Proposed and Implemented Action

任何计划的基础都在于人们采取的基本行动。要详细描述行动的构成要素，往往只能给出一个大致的概括。计划可以是粗略的，由大型行动组成；也可以是精细的，由小型行动组成。行动可以具有一系列属性，例如参与者、时间以及地点。鉴于这些粗略的属性，我们很难提供更详细的描述，只能提供参与者、时间参考和地点这几个最通用的术语，如图 8.1 所示。

The basis of any plan consists of the fundamental actions that people take. It is difficult to give any more than an outline description of what makes up an action. A plan can be coarse, consisting of large actions, or it can be finegrained, consisting of small actions. Actions can have a range of properties, based on who, when, and where. With such coarse-grained properties it is difficult to provide more than the most generic terms of party, time reference, and location, as shown in Figure 8.1.

图 8.1 动作的属性。

Figure 8.1 Properties of actions.

在制定和监控计划时，我们必须考虑一项行动可能经历的多种状态。它可以被安排、分配资源、配备人员、启动和完成。状态转换图可以记录这些状态以及转换的发生方式。很难对这些转换制定任何规则。安排行动和分配资源显然可以按任意顺序进行。表面分析可能会得出结论：行动不能在资源分配和安排之前启动。那么，我们该如何处理在正式确定行动时间之前就已经启动的行动呢？我们可以辩称，这类行动是在启动前不久才被安排的，但这听起来更像是管理理论的合理化解释，而不是对实际业务流程的反映。另一个问题是部分资源分配。任何项目经理都会告诉你，在现实世界中，任务经常在所有必需资源分配完毕之前就开始了。我们如何在行动状态的描述中反映这种情况呢？

When making and monitoring plans, we must consider the many states that an action can go through. It can be scheduled, resourced, peopled, started, and completed. A state-transition diagram can record these states and how the transitions can occur. It is difficult to make any rules about these transitions. Scheduling an action and resourcing it can clearly happen in any order. A surface analysis may conclude that an action cannot be started before resourcing and scheduling. How do we deal with actions that are started before any formal decision is made to state a time for them? We could argue that such actions are scheduled a moment before they are started, but this sounds more like a management theory rationalization than a reflection of the real business process. Another problem arises with partial resourcing. Any project manager will tell you that in the real world, tasks are often begun before all the required resources are allocated. How can we reflect this situation in descriptions of action states?

如图 8.2 所示，行动的两个重要状态是提议行动和已实施行动。提议行动仅仅是计划中的一个提案。因此，可以通过添加时间参考点来安排行动进度，通过添加参与方来获取资源，并指定相应的位置。这些更改可以随时按任意顺序进行。一旦行动开始，它就进入了实施阶段。这不仅改变了行动状态，而且还会创建一个单独的已实施行动对象。这使我们能够记录计划与实施之间的差异。通过保留原始的提议行动，我们可以看到计划与实际情况之间的差异。例如，一个常见的差异是时间参考点；然而，随着计划文档最终转化为行动，任何属性都可能发生改变。

The two important states of action are proposed and implemented actions, as shown in Figure 8.2. A proposed action is purely a proposal that exists in some plan. As such it can be scheduled by adding a time reference, resourced by adding parties, and located with the appropriate location. These changes can be made at any time, in any order. Once an action is begun, it is implemented. Not only is this a change in state, but also a separate implemented action object is created. This allows us to record differences between plan and implementation. By retaining the original proposed action, we can see the differences between the plan and reality. A common difference, for example, is the time reference; however, any attribute can change as planning documents finally turn into actions.

图 8.2 计划和行动的基本结构。

Figure 8.2 Basic structure of plans and actions.

将提案和实施方案分别记录在不同的文件中，以便 跟踪差异。

Separate objects record the proposal and the implementation so that differences can be tracked.

例如，我决定在 1997 年 7 月 1 日为 OOPSLA 准备一个演示文稿，但我直到 7 月 3 日才开始着手准备。这些行动可以表示为一个日期为 7 月 1 日的提议行动和一个日期为 7 月 3 日的已实施行动。提议的所有其他属性均相同。

Example I decide to prepare a presentation for OOPSLA on July 1, 1997, but I don't get around to doing it until the 3rd. These actions can be represented as a proposed action with a date of July 1 and an implemented action with a date of July 3. All other attributes of the proposal are the same.

我们可以提供一个派生的动作状态属性，以便更轻松地判断一个动作所处的状态，而无需遍历记录其状态的各种结构。虽然在现阶段这并非必要，但随着我们后续考虑其他结构，它的价值将日益凸显。

We can provide a derived action state property to make it easier to tell what state an action is in without navigating the various structures that record its state. This is not really necessary at this stage but becomes valuable as we consider additional structures later.

为了在记录日常行动时保持最大的灵活性，如图 8.2 所示，计划行动与已实施行动之间的关联是可选的。很多时候，即使是最好的计划也会因为缺乏执行而束之高阁，许多行动甚至在没有任何事先计划的情况下发生。我们应该抵制为临时计划寻找合理性的诱惑。

To retain the best degree of flexibility in recording daily actions, the links between proposed action and implemented action, as shown in Figure 8.2, are optional. Often the best laid plans gather dust without implementation, and many actions occur without any prior planning. We should resist the temptation to rationalize last-minute plans.

例如，瑟兹医生为约翰·史密斯开了全血细胞计数检查单，但病人没有来做检查。这代表一项已提出的行动，但尚未实施。如果病人被重新预约到稍后的日期，这就构成了一项新的已提出的行动。

Example Doctor Thursz orders a full blood count for John Smith, but the patient does not turn up for the test. This represents a proposed action without an implemented action. If the patient is rebooked for a later date, this constitutes a new proposed action.

例如，凯恩斯医生被叫去诊治一位在火车上突然生病的女士。这里已经采取了行动，但没有提出行动方案。

Example Doctor Cairns is called to attend a woman who is taken suddenly ill on a train. Here there is an implemented action but no proposed action.

8.2 已完成和已放弃的行动

8.2 Completed and Abandoned Actions

到目前为止，我们已经探讨了行动的提出和启动方式，但尚未探讨行动的结束方式。显然，行动要么成功，要么失败。问题在于，我们常常无法确定行动的成功或失败，尤其是在医疗保健领域。因此，本节仅讨论两种结束行动：完成和放弃。完成是指行动按照计划执行。对成功或失败的任何考量都将留待后续分析（参见第 8.7 节）。对于医疗保健以外的领域，这种定义可能过于严格，因为在医疗保健领域，成功更容易判断。区分按预期执行行动和行动实现其目标仍然十分重要。

So far we have considered how actions are proposed and begin but not how they might end. Clearly actions either succeed or fail. The problem is that often we cannot determine success or failure with any certainty, especially in health care. Thus in this section we consider only two ending actions: completion and abandonment. Completion occurs when the action is carried out according to plan. Any consideration of the success or failure is left to further analysis (see Section 8.7). This definition can be too strict for domains other than health care, where success is more easily judged. The distinction between carrying out an action as expected and the action achieving its goal is still valuable.

图 8.3 已完成和已放弃的行动。

Figure 8.3 Completed and abandoned actions.

放弃是指彻底且最终地停止某项行动。它可以发生在行动开始实施之前，也可以发生在行动开始实施之后。放弃一项拟议的行动意味着决定根本不开始实施。

Abandonment is a complete and final cessation of the action. It can occur either before or after beginning to implement the action. Abandoning a proposed action is deciding not to begin it at all.

例如，肾移植手术通过用捐献的健康肾脏替换受损肾脏来恢复肾功能。如果肾脏安全移植到受者体内，则肾移植手术被视为成功。如果肾脏之后出现排异反应，这并不影响移植手术的成功。移植手术仍然算完成；只有在手术过程中出现问题时，才会判定手术失败。

Example A renal transplant provides renal function by replacing a damaged kidney with a donated working kidney. The renal transplant action is judged a success if the kidney is safely transplanted into the recipient. If the kidney is rejected later, this does not invalidate the success of the transplant procedure. The transplant procedure is still completed; it would be abandoned only if a problem occurs during the operation.

例如，我选择从伦敦飞往波士顿，预计下午2点到达。航班延误，所以我直到晚上7点才到达。尽管如此，这项行动仍然算完成，因为我当天到达了波士顿。但由于延误，这项行动并未成功。然而，我原计划当晚外出就餐的行动却被取消了。

Example I chose to fly from London to Boston, expecting to arrive in Boston at 2:00 p.m. The flight is delayed, so I did not arrive until 7:00 p.m. This action was still completed, because I arrived in Boston that day. The delay I suffered meant that it was not a success. The proposed action to go to dinner that evening, however, was abandoned.

例如：我的车发动不了，我判断是起动电机坏了。于是我决定更换起动电机。刚开始不久，我就发现问题其实出在连接不良上，起动电机本身没问题。虽然我对这个结果并不失望，但我还是放弃了更换起动电机的计划！

Example My car would not start, and I determined the problem was a faulty starter motor. I thus proposed and began to replace the starter motor. Just after beginning I found that the fault was actually a bad connection, and the starter motor was fine. I thus abandoned the action of replacing the starter motor, although I was not unhappy with the result!

8.3 悬架

8.3 Suspension

我们也可以推迟某些行动，打算以后再继续。

We can also put off actions, with the intention of continuing them later.

如图 8.4 所示，当这种情况发生时，暂停状态会与该行动关联起来。暂停状态在其有效期限内有效（该期限可能没有上限）。如果行动在暂停期结束后继续进行，则暂停状态仍然存在，但不再处于暂停状态，行动继续进行。

When this occurs a suspension is linked to the action, as shown in Figure 8.4. The suspension is valid within its time period (which might be open ended). If an action continues after the end point of the suspension, the suspension still exists but is no longer suspending, and the action continues.

图 8.4 暂停行动。

Figure 8.4 Suspension of actions.

中止是指暂时中止某项行动。

A suspension is a temporary hold on an action.

因此，如果一项行动目前处于暂停状态，则该行动将被暂停。已提出的行动和已实施的行动均可被暂停；暂停一项已提出的行动相当于推迟该行动的开始时间。

Thus an action is suspended if it has currently open suspension. Both proposed and implemented actions can be suspended; suspending a proposed action is equivalent to postponing the start of an action.

例如，一位患者正在等待肾移植。这可以用肾移植的意向来表示。患者必须等待合适的肾源出现。如果患者在等待期间患上感冒，医生必须暂停患者的移植等待。由于患者在感冒痊愈后会重新回到等待名单上，因此移植手术并未被放弃。暂停移植的记录对于解释医生为何在此期间没有为患者提供合适的肾源至关重要。

Example A patient is on the waiting list for a renal transplant. This is represented by a proposed action of renal transplant. The patient has to wait for a kidney to become available. If the patient develops a cold while on the waiting list, the doctor must place a suspension on the patient. The transplant is not abandoned because the patient goes back on the waiting list when the cold abates. The record of the suspension is essential to explain why the doctor did not give a suitable kidney to the patient during that time.

例如，我有一个洗碗的计划。这个计划经常被搁置很长时间，但我从来没有彻底放弃过它！

Example I have a proposed action to wash the dishes. It is frequently suspended for long periods, but I never quite abandon it!

8.4 计划

8.4 Plan

简而言之，计划就是一系列按一定顺序排列的行动方案。顺序可以用多种方式表达，但最常见的是依赖关系——即一个行动必须在另一个行动完成后才能开始。计划通常使用依赖关系图来描述，例如关键路径分析。

In its simplest sense a plan is a collection of proposed actions linked in some sequence. A sequence can be expressed in a number of ways, but most commonly it is expressed as a dependency—an indication that one action cannot begin until another completes. Plans are often described by using a dependency diagram, as in critical path analysis.

图 8.5 展示了拟议行动之间的依赖关系图。当行动始终作为单一计划的一部分提出时，这种结构非常有用。然而，在许多情况下，计划之间会相互影响。例如，当医生为患者制定治疗计划时，护士会使用该治疗计划中的行动来制定她们的护理计划。许多护理人员为患者制定计划的情况并不少见，因此，确保这些计划协调一致至关重要。图 8.6 所示的结构支持交互，它允许在多个计划中引用同一行动，并且依赖关系是在引用之间而非行动之间建立的。

Figure 8.5 is a diagram of a dependency relationship between proposed actions. This structure is useful when the actions are always proposed as part of a single plan. In many situations, however, plans interact. When a doctor sets up a treatment plan for a patient, actions within that treatment plan are used by the nurses in setting up their nursing plans. It is not unusual for many caregivers to have plans for a patient, and it is important that these plans be properly choreographed. The structure shown in Figure 8.6 supports interaction by allowing an action to be referenced within multiple plans and for the dependencies to be drawn up between the references rather than between the actions.

图 8.5 建议行动之间的依赖关系。

Figure 8.5 Dependencies between proposed actions.

这将只允许在一个计划内提出行动方案，使得 计划协调变得困难。

This will only allow actions to be proposed within one plan, making it difficult to coordinate plans.

例如，一位医生需要为病人做全血细胞计数。她查看了拟定的治疗方案列表，发现另一位医生已经在他的治疗计划中包含了全血细胞计数。这表示另一位医生的治疗计划中包含一个指向全血细胞计数的治疗方案的操作引用。可以创建一个新的治疗计划，并添加一个指向同一治疗方案的新操作引用。

Example A doctor needs a full blood count for a patient. She checks the list of proposed actions and finds that another doctor has already proposed a full blood count as part of his plan. This is represented as the other doctor's plan having an action reference to the full blood count proposed action. A new plan can be created with a new action reference to the same proposed action.

图 8.6 包含拟议行动参考的计划。

Figure 8.6 A plan consisting of references to proposed actions. This

该结构允许多个计划引用行动。

structure allows actions to be referenced by several plans.

例如，我需要去酒铺买些圣埃米利翁（St. Emillion）葡萄酒，周六晚上要参加晚宴，还要买些老怪味（Old Peculiar）葡萄酒，周日要参加派对。去酒铺这一行为在晚宴准备计划和派对计划中都有提及。晚宴准备计划中提到去酒铺是因果关系，参加晚宴是结果，去酒铺是因果关系。派对计划中提到去酒铺是因果关系，开始派对是结果，去酒铺是因果关系。

Example I need to visit the liquor store to get some St. Emillion for a dinner on Saturday and Old Peculiar for a party on Sunday. The action of visiting the liquor store is referenced in both the plan for preparing for the dinner and the plan for the party. The dinner preparation's reference has a dependency where attending the dinner is the consequent and visiting the liquor store is the dependent. The party plan's reference has a dependency where beginning the party is the consequent and the visit to the liquor store is the dependent.

在行为描述中，动作及其引用的概念是行为建模中的常见模式。它类似于子程序的定义及其在另一个子程序中的调用。子程序的定义不包含任何关于其在调用程序中如何使用的信息。调用程序也对子程序的具体内容一无所知。

This notion of an action and a reference to an action within behavioral description is a common pattern in behavioral modeling. It is analogous to the definition of a subroutine and its call within another subroutine. The definition of the subroutine contains no information on how it is used within a calling program. The calling program has no knowledge of the contents of the subroutine.

图 8.6 中的模型是一个简单的行为元模型。计划是对预期行为的描述，因此行为建模技术是合适的。我们可以使用任何行为建模技术。首先，我们用元模型来表示该技术。然后，我们将元模型中的动作与计划对象以及建议的动作关联起来。我们应该选择一个既精细又不至于过于复杂的行为模型。

The model in Figure 8.6 is a simple behavioral meta-model. A plan is a description of intended behavior, thus a behavioral modeling technique is appropriate. We can use any behavioral modeling technique. First we represent the technique by its meta-model. Then we tie the actions of the meta-model to the plan object and to the proposed actions. We should choose a behavioral model that is sophisticated without being overly complex.

计划总是会发生变化，并且可以被其他计划取代，如图 8.7 所示。这种关联在两个方向上都是多值的——随着计划的变化，一个计划可以被拆分并被单独的计划取代，或者几个计划可以合并成一个计划。

Plans are always subject to change and can be replaced by other plans, as shown in Figure 8.7. The association is multivalued in both directions—as plans change, a single plan can be split up and replaced by separate plans, or several plans can be consolidated into one.

图 8.7 更换方案。

Figure 8.7 Replacement plans.

例如，我原本计划在伊甸园买面包，在面包与马戏团买奶酪。现在我把这个计划改为在杰氏餐厅买外卖。

Example I have a plan to buy bread at the Garden of Eden and cheese at Bread and Circus. I replace this by a plan to get a take-away from Jae's instead.

我们可以将计划视为行动的一种子类型，如图 8.8 所示。因此，我们可以提出计划（即，我们可以为计划制定计划），并监控计划的完成情况。由于计划制定通常相当复杂，因此能够安排和跟踪计划的进展就显得尤为重要。

We can consider a plan to be a subtype of an action, as shown in Figure 8.8. Thus we can propose a plan (that is, we can plan for a plan) and monitor a plan to see if it is finished. Since planning is often quite complex, it is valuable to be able to schedule and track a plan's progress.

图 8.8 计划即行动和复合行动。

Figure 8.8 Plans as actions and compound actions.

我们可以制定计划，也可以在没有明确计划的情况下采取复杂的行动。

We can plan to plan, and we can have complex actions without an explicit plan.

我们可以将计划视为一种聚合行动的方式。例如，全血细胞计数可以表示为一个计划，其中每个组成部分的测量结果都代表计划中的一个拟议行动。然而，这种表示方法过于简单粗暴。图 8.8 所示的结构也允许将一个行动分解为组成行动，但它提供了两种表示行动作为更大行动一部分的方式：对于简单情况，使用父组件关联效果很好；对于更复杂情况，使用计划效果很好。我们可以将父组件关联限制在一个层级结构中，这样父组件关联就只用于简单情况。

We can think of a plan as a way of aggregating actions. For example, a full blood count can be represented as a plan, with each component measurement as a proposed action within it. This is a very heavy-handed representation, however. The structure shown in Figure 8.8 also allows an action to be decomposed into component actions, but it allows two ways to represent actions being part of a larger action: Using the parent-component association works well for simple cases, and using a plan works well for more complex cases. We can restrict the parent-component association to a hierarchy so only the parent-component association is used for simple cases.

8.5 协议

8.5 Protocol

组织的标准操作程序是指多次重复执行的常见操作，每次执行的方式都大同小异。我们可以用类似于描述计划的结构来描述这些常见操作（这里称为协议），如图 8.9 所示。计划模式，如同本书中的其他模式一样，可以分为知识层和操作层。操作层描述日常计划和行动。知识层包含协议，协议描述了指导操作层的标准程序。

An organization's standard operating procedures are common actions carried out many times in much the same way each time. We can describe these common actions, referred to here as protocols, using constructs similar to those we used for plans, as shown in Figure 8.9. Planning patterns, like other patterns in this book, can be divided into knowledge and operational levels. The operational levels describe the day-to-day plans and actions. At the knowledge level are protocols, which describe the standard procedures that guide the operational level.

图 8.9 协议结构。

Figure 8.9 Structure for protocols.

它的结构与计划的结构类似——一个简单的行为元模型。

It is a similar structure as the one for plans — a simple behavioral meta-model.

知识层和操作层在结构上存在一些有趣的差异。在知识层，使用层级结构的作用要小得多。协议可以被许多其他协议引用；很难想象有什么情况下限制协议的引用会是有益的。当我们想要以常规方式聚合操作时，例如将测量值作为全血细胞计数的一部分，我们通常可以有效地将一个操作表示为另一个操作的一部分。

There are some interesting differences between the knowledge and operational levels in the structure. Using a hierarchic structure is much less useful at the knowledge level. Protocol can be referenced by many other protocols; it is hard to think of a case where restricting it would be useful. We can often effectively represent an action as part of another action in cases where we want to aggregate actions in a regular manner, such as the measurement as part of a full blood count.

在知识层面上，拟议行动和已实施行动之间没有区别，计划和另一组行动之间也没有实质性的区别。协议的组成部分始终是一个整体（因为一个协议可以在另一个协议中多次执行），但计划中拟议的行动始终构成一个集合（因为你不能重复执行同一个行动，但你可以使用同一个协议执行两个行动）。

There is no difference at the knowledge level between proposed and implemented actions, nor is there a valuable distinction between a plan and another group of actions. The components of a protocol are always a bag (since a protocol can be performed more than once within another), but the proposed actions of a plan always form a set (since you cannot do the same action twice, but you can have two actions with the same protocol).

协议无需详细描述其组成部分。协议可以仅仅是一个名称，可以是描述、教科书页面、网页，甚至是演示某个复杂外科手术的视频。协议引用可以只描述组成部分，而无需任何依赖关系。有些协议可以完全用代码编写到计算机中，在这种情况下，它们就成为一段软件。（软件协议是指用软件编写的协议，而不是通信协议意义上的协议。）

A protocol need not be detailed with components. A protocol can be merely a name. It can be descriptions, textbook pages, Web pages, even a video of someone performing a particularly tricky surgical procedure. Protocol references can just describe components without any dependencies. Some protocols can be entirely coded into a computer, in which case they become a piece of software. (A software protocol is a protocol that is coded in software, not a protocol in the sense of a communications protocol.]

我们可以通过两种方式从复杂的协议中生成操作。最简单的方法是使用父组件关联。当所有组件操作都在明确的时间段内执行，且无人想要共享组件操作时，这种方法非常有效。我们首先为整个协议创建一个建议的操作，只有在需要指定特定属性（例如时间或资源）时才指定组件操作。（如果这类特定属性很多，则应该使用计划。）如果所有操作都由同一方在大致相同的时间执行，则父操作就足够了。每个组件协议的引用都会创建一个组件操作；也就是说，在父协议中执行三次的协议将产生三个组件操作；任何依赖关系都将与协议中完全相同。

We can form actions from a complex protocol in two ways. The simplest way is to use the parent-component association. This technique works well when the component actions all take place in a well-bounded time period, and no one wants to share the component actions. We first create a proposed action for the whole protocol and only indicate the component actions if we have to specify particular properties, such as timing or resources. (If there are a lot of these particular properties, then we should use a plan.) If all actions are done by the same party at about the same time, the parent action is enough. A component action is created for each component protocol's reference; that is, a protocol carried out three times within a parent protocol would yield three component actions; any dependencies would exist exactly as in the protocol.

计划能够提供更大的灵活性和更精确的跟踪，因此，当我们想要监控各个流程步骤的执行时间和方式时，计划是更佳的选择。这些关系如图 8.10 所示。此外，计划允许组件建议的操作被其他计划拾取和共享。计划的一个重要特性是，它们不仅可以复制流程的依赖关系，还可以定义新的依赖关系，这些依赖关系可能忽略流程中的依赖关系。这种能力在医疗保健等专业领域尤为重要，因为我们经常需要根据患者的个体需求来调整流程。我们经常需要一次性计划，这些计划基于流程，但并非流程的完全复制。

A plan offers greater flexibility and precision of tracking and thus is preferred when we want to monitor when and how individual protocol steps are carried out. These relationships are shown in Figure 8.10. In addition, a plan allows the component proposed actions to be picked up and shared with other plans. An important feature of plans is that, while they can copy the dependencies of the protocol, plans can also define new dependencies that might ignore that of the protocol. This ability is important in skilled professions such as health care, where we often have to override protocols to take into account the needs of individual patients. Frequently we need one-off plans, which are based on protocols but are not faithful copies.

根据协议制定行动通常会在协议的较高层级使用计划，并在较低层级使用父组件关联。

Forming actions from a protocol will typically use plans at higher levels of the protocol, and use the parent-component association at lower levels.

8.5.1 以图的形式呈现计划和协议

我们还可以将计划表示为拟议行动的有向无环图 (DAG)。图中的弧对应于行动引用的依赖关系。每个计划都有其独立的图结构。我们可以将其简洁地表示为如图 8.11 所示。本质上，这是第 15 章中描述的另一种关联模式。

We can also represent a plan as a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of proposed actions. The arcs on the graph correspond to the dependency relationships on the action references. Each plan has its own separate graph structure. We can represent this compactly as shown in Figure 8.11. This is, in essence, another association pattern in the style described in Chapter 15.

然而，要将此概念应用于协议，我们并不构建子协议的有向无环图 (DAG)。相反，我们构建协议引用的有向无环图，如图 8.12 所示，因为一个协议可以包含多个步骤。

To apply this notion to a protocol, however, we do not form a DAG of the subsidiary protocols. Instead we form a DAG of the protocol references, as shown in Figure 8.12, because one protocol can appear as more than one step

图 8.10 行动、计划和协议之间的关系。

Figure 8.10 Relationships among action, plan, and protocol.

图 8.11 将计划表示为拟议行动的有向无环图。

Figure 8.11 Plan as a directed acyclic graph of proposed actions.

在另一个父协议中。但对于计划而言，情况并非如此，因为存在图 8.6 所示的唯一性约束。因此，DAG 关联模式的基本形式包括依赖类型（带有约束），以及 DAG 中的元素只能作为 DAG 中的一个节点出现这一事实。

in another parent protocol. This is specifically not the case for a plan due to the uniqueness constraint shown in Figure 8.6. The base form for a DAG association pattern thus includes the dependency types (with the constraint) together with the fact that the element in the DAG can only appear as one node in a DAG.

图 8.12 使用 DAG 的协议。

Figure 8.12 Protocol using a DAG.

如果我们使用图来表示计划结构，就会失去建立图 8.10 中所示的计划引用和协议引用之间关联的能力。当然，我们仍然可以使用 DAG 版本作为派生映射；派生过程将包括如何导出图的弧。

If we use a graph for the plan structure we lose the ability to build the association between the plan reference and the protocol reference that is shown in Figure 8.10. Naturally we could still have the DAG version as a derived mapping; the derivation would include how to derive the graph's arcs.

8.6 资源分配

8.6 Resource Allocation

规划的第二个主要部分是资源分配。拟议行动和已实施行动的主要区别在于它们如何使用资源。已实施的行动会实际使用分配给它的资源，而拟议行动只是预定一些资源。图 8.13 显示了资源分配，资源分配以某种资源类型的数量表示。资源只能由一个行动预定，也只能由一个行动使用。

The second major part of planning is allocating resources. A primary difference between proposed and implemented actions lies in how they use resources. An implemented action will actually use resources allocated to it. A proposed action will book some resources. Figure 8.13 shows resource allocation as a quantity of some resource type. Resources can only be booked by one action and used by one action.

图 8.13 行动对资源的使用。

Figure 8.13 Action's use of resources.

拟议行动需要资源，而已实施的行动需要使用资源。

Proposed actions book resources, and implemented actions use resources.

资源种类繁多。最主要也是最常见的是消耗品。消耗品包括药品、针头和原材料等。消耗品只能使用一次，使用后即被消耗殆尽。通常情况下，消耗品是按数量索取的。

There are various kinds of resources. The first and most obvious is a consumable. Consumables are such things as drugs, needles, and raw materials. Consumables can be used only once and are used up by the action that uses them. Typically consumables are asked for by quantity.

例如， 10 加仑橙汁的资源分配，数量为 10 加仑，资源类型为橙汁。

Example A resource allocation of 10 gallons of orange juice has a quantity of 10 gallons and resource type of orange juice.

例如，某次髋关节置换手术预定了四单位浓缩红细胞（血液），但实际只用了两单位。这可以用两份浓缩红细胞资源分配来表示。一份分配对应​​拟进行的髋关节置换手术，数量为四单位；另一份分配对应​​已完成的髋关节置换手术，数量为两单位。

Example For a particular hip replacement operation, four units of packed red cells (blood) are booked, but only two are used. This can be represented by two resource allocations of the resource type packed red cells. One is linked to the proposed hip replacement with quantity four units; the other is linked to the implemented hip replacement with quantity two units.

有些资源不会被消耗，例如设备、房间和人力。从任何意义上说，人都不会被行动消耗掉（尽管写完这本书后我开始怀疑这一点）。然而，我们可以说人的时间会被消耗掉。在这种情况下，资源类型是人，数量是时间。因此，我花五个小时做某件事，就是我投入了五个小时的资源。

Some resources are not consumed, such as equipment, rooms, and people. In no sense is a person consumed by an action (although after writing this book I wonder). However, we can say that a person's time is used up. In this case the resource type is the person, and the quantity is time. Thus my spending five hours on an action is a resource allocation of five hours of me.

这种对资源类型的理解未免过于个人化。资源类型属于知识层面，通常指的是事物的种类，而非事物本身。我参与的项目需要的是一位经验丰富的面向对象建模师，而不是我个人，他们通常需要五个小时的工作。虽然有些人足够独特，本身就是一种资源类型，但我们大多数人只是众多资源类型中的一员。

This is somewhat too individual a view of resource types. Resource types, which lie at the knowledge level, more typically indicate a kind of thing rather than the thing itself. Projects that I work on demand five hours of an experienced OO modeler rather than me in particular. Although some people are sufficiently singular to be resource types in their own right, most of us mortals are merely one of many.

因此，在规划阶段，需求被表述为“我们需要一位面向对象建模师，工作时长为五小时”。在规划过程的某个阶段，这个问题通过预订我本人（即该资源类型的一个特定实例）的五小时工作时间来解决。这意味着资源分配分为两个层次：一个是仅指定资源类型的通用分配，另一个是指定具体人员的专属分配。

In planning, therefore, the requirement is stated as "We need five hours of an OO modeler." At some stage in the planning process, this is resolved by booking five hours of me, a specific instance of the resource type. This implies two levels of resource allocation: a general one where only the type is specified and a specific allocation where the individual is specified.

在图 8.14 中，个体被视为一种资产。资产按资产类型分类，而资产类型本身就是一种资源类型。

In Figure 8.14 the individual is referred to as an asset. Assets are classified by asset type, which is just a kind of resource type. The difference

图 8.14 资产资源分配。

Figure 8.14 Resource allocations for assets.

特定分配指明所使用的或已记录的具体资产。一般分配仅 指定资产类型。

Specific allocations name the individual asset used or booked. General allocations only specify the type of asset.

特定资源类型与通用资源类型的区别在于，前者关联到资产，后者关联到资源类型（对于资产而言，该资源类型即为资产类型）。临时资源是资产的特定资源分配。它不仅可以包含一定时间，还可以包含特定的时间段。该时间段可以从预订或使用临时资源的操作中得出，也可以是独立存在的。

between a specific resource type and a general resource type is that the former links to the asset and the latter to a resource type, which for an asset would be an asset type. A temporal resource is a specific resource allocation of an asset. It can have not just an amount of time but also a specific time period. This period can be derived from the action that books or uses the temporal resource, or it can be separate.

例如，一个建模会议计划在小型会议室举行几个小时。最初，这被表示为一项预定行动，该行动会预订一个通用资源分配。该通用资源分配的资源类型为“小型会议室”，资源量为两小时。之后，实际的会议室被预订为 Q9。这会将通用资源分配重新分类（或替换）为 Q9 资产的临时资源，时长为两小时。如果会议预定时间为周二下午 2:00 至 5:00，则该时间段即为 Q9 资源分配的派生时间段。如果会议的最后一小时安排在酒吧举行，则周二下午 2:00 至 4:00 的时间段将与该临时资源关联。

Example A modeling meeting is scheduled to be held in a small conference room for a couple of hours. Initially this is represented as a proposed action that books a general resource allocation. The resource type of the general resource allocation is the asset type small conference room. The quantity of the general resource allocation is two hours. At some later point the actual conference room is booked as Q9. This reclassif ies (or replaces) the general resource allocation to a temporal resource of two hours of the asset Q9. If the proposed action of the meeting is booked between 2:00 and 5:00 p.m. on Tuesday, then that time period is the derived time period of the allocation of Q9. If the last hour of the meeting is to be held in the pub, then a time period of 2:00 to 4:00 p.m. on Tuesday is linked to the temporal resource.

一项资产可以拥有多种资产类型。这种资产的多重分类对于体现那些能够执行多种功能的资产至关重要，尽管这些功能不一定能够同时实现。

The asset is allowed to have several asset types. This multiple classification of assets is important to represent those assets that can do several things, although not necessarily at once.

例如，如果会议室 Q9 配备投影设备，则既可以将其归类为小型会议室，也可以将其归类为演示室。但不能通过不同的操作同时将其预订为这两种用途。

Example If the conference room Q9 has projection facilities, it can be classified as both a small conference room and a presentation room. It cannot be booked as both at the same time by separate actions.

对于消耗品而言，具体的资源分配并不那么重要。例如，通常只需说明某项活动记录并使用了 10 加仑橙汁即可，无需具体说明是哪 10 加仑。但对于资产，我们通常需要具体说明，因为各方之间更容易就资产的使用产生争议。

Specific resource allocation is less important for consumables. For example, it is usually enough to say that 10 gallons of orange juice were booked and used by an action without being more specific about which 10 gallons. With assets we usually need to be specific because there is a greater likelihood for contention between parties about use of assets.

此时值得考虑的是，图 8.13 中所示的操作子类型之间的关系是否应该进行专门化。例如，可以合理地规定，已执行的操作只能使用特定的资产资源分配。假设这是必要的（我不确定这是否普遍适用），那么有几种方法可以实现。这很好地说明了如何以不同的方式对业务规则进行建模。

At this point it is worth considering whether the relationships from subtypes of the action shown in Figure 8.13 should be specialized. For example, it may be reasonable to say that implemented actions can only use specific resource allocations of assets. Assuming that this is something that is required (and I'm not sure that it is in general), there are several ways of doing it. This brings up a good example of how a business rule can be modeled in different ways.

第一种方法，也是最显而易见的方法，是引入结构性约束。例如，我们可以使用类似“已执行的操作不能使用资源类型为资产类型的通用资源分配”这样的规则。这种主动检查是一种强制执行业务规则的激进方式。它表明，不允许记录违反策略的情况。

The first, and most obvious, way is to introduce a structural constraint. In this case we can use a rule such as "Implemented actions cannot use general resource allocations whose resource type is an asset type." This eager checking is an aggressive way to enforce the business rule. It says that you are not allowed to record a situation that violates the policy.

然而，这种方法有时过于强硬。有时，允许记录违反策略的情况，并在之后进行单独的检查阶段，才是合理的。这种延迟检查可以通过对已实现的操作（例如 isConsistentQ）进行某种操作来实现，如果业务规则得到遵守，则该操作返回 true。这为处理一开始可能无法获得完整约束的情况提供了更大的灵活性。不完整的信息会被记录下来，并提供一种检查方法。

This can be too strong a way to do things, however. Sometimes it makes sense to allow a situation that violates the policy to be recorded, and to have a separate checking phase later. This lazy checking can be done by having some operation on implemented action (such as isConsistentQ) and having that operation return true if the business rule is followed. This provides greater flexibility in handling situations where a full constraint might not be available from the beginning. The incomplete information is recorded, and a means for checking it is provided.

延迟检查的最大优势在于它将问题的解决与信息的记录分开。记录信息的人员可以尽力而为，之后可以由他们自己或更专业的人员进行澄清。如果在信息采集阶段就能轻松解决问题，那么积极检查则更为理想。

The great advantage of lazy checking is that it separates the resolution of the problem from the recording of the information. People recording the information can make their best attempt at the time, and then either they or a more qualified person can clear things up later. If matters can be resolved easily at the point of information capture, then eager checking is better.

是否允许对已实施的行动进行一般资源分配，取决于具体问题。如果只需知道某个面向对象建模人员花费了两个小时，而无需知道具体是哪位建模人员，就能满足领域需求，那么就应该允许对资产类型进行一般分配。这个问题可能取决于资产类型。例如，医院政策可能规定，所有顾问的分配都必须具体明确，而护理员的分配则可以一般进行。

Whether to allow general resource allocation of assets to implemented actions depends on the specific problem. If the needs of the domain are satisfied by knowing that it took two hours of an OO modeler without knowing which one, then general allocation of asset types should be allowed. This question may be dependent on the asset type. For example, hospital policy may dictate that all implemented allocations of consultants must be specific, although orderlies may be allocated generally.

如果我们需要跟踪某个有限存储空间中的消耗品，就可以使用特定的资源分配方式。在这种情况下，我们希望表明消耗品是从该消耗品的特定存储单元中取出的，如图 8.15 所示。存储单元可以是……

We can use specific resource allocation with consumables if we are concerned with removing the consumable from some finite store that we have to track. In such cases we want to say that the consumable is taken from a particular holding of that consumable, as shown in Figure 8.15. Holdings can be

图 8.15 允许对消耗品进行特定分配。

Figure 8.15 Allowing specific allocations of consumables.

根据资源跟踪流程的不同（此处暂不讨论），其组织方式多种多样。但值得一提的是，根据第 6.14 节所述的方法，持仓可以视为一个账户，资源分配可以视为一个条目。

organized in various ways, depending on the resource tracking process, which I am not considering here. However, it is worth saying that a holding can be seen as an account and a resource allocation as an entry, following the approach described in Section 6.14.

协议也可以使用资源分配来描述执行协议所需的资源。在这种情况下，我们使用通用资源分配。

Resource allocations can also be used by protocols to describe the resources needed for a protocol to be carried out. In this case we use general resource allocations.

例如，制作印度薄饼（chapati）需要 4 杯面粉、8 杯水、4 汤匙油和一小撮盐。这可以表示为四种一般资源分配。

Example To make chapati (Indian bread) you need V4 cup of flour, V8 cup of water, V4 tablespoon of oil, and a pinch of salt. This can be represented as four general resource allocations.

8.7 结果和开始函数

8.7 Outcome and Start Functions

在本节中，我们将运用第 3 章中提出的概念来思考我们制定计划的原因以及如何衡量计划的成功。

In this section we use concepts developed in Chapter 3 to consider reasons why we form a plan and how we can gauge its success.

计划的制定源于观察，而这些观察当然可以是假设或预测。同样，计划的结果也是与计划内行动相关的观察，如图 8.16 所示。与观察的许多方面一样，结果的关联性取决于执行者的视角。因此，有些人可能不会将某个观察结果视为行动的结果，而另一些人则会。我们会通过让不同的执行者进行多次观察来记录这种情况。

Plans are initiated by observations, which, of course, can be hypotheses or projections. Similarly their outcomes are observations linked to the actions within the plan, as shown in Figure 8.16. Like many aspects of observation, the outcome link is dependent on the eyes of the performer. Thus some parties may not see an observation as the outcome of an action while others would. We would record this situation by having more than one observation by different performers.

图 8.16 观察、计划和行动之间的联系。

Figure 8.16 Links between observation, plan, and action.

例如，约翰·史密斯因出现典型的糖尿病症状——体重减轻、口渴和多尿——而就诊。医生根据这些观察结果制定了一套诊疗方案，其中包括一项建议：进行血糖测量。

Example John Smith came to his doctor with the classic symptoms of diabetes: weight loss, thirst, and polyuria. The doctor creates a plan triggered by these observations. The plan includes a proposed action to carry out a blood glucose measurement.

例如，一家公司在销售业绩不佳后，决定提高销售人员的佣金并降低产品价格。一些分析师可能会认为销售额的提升是佣金提高的结果，而另一些分析师则可能认为销售额的提升是价格降低的结果。两组分析师会分别进行观察，并将结果与​​不同的措施联系起来。

Example After experiencing poor sales, a company decides to improve the sales force's commission and to cut prices. Some analysts might say that the improved sales were the outcome of the increase in commission, others might say the improvement was the outcome of the cut in prices. Separate observations would be made by each group, with links to different actions.

请注意，观察是行动的一种子类型。观察可以安排时间、设定时间、由执行者进行，并且可以成为计划的一部分。观察的另一个作用是识别观察概念或测量现象类型。

Note that observations are a subtype of actions. They can be scheduled, timed, have performers, and be parts of plans. Their additional behavior is that they identify an observation concept or measure a phenomenon type.

如图 8.17 所示，在知识层面也存在类似的关联，即起始函数和结果函数。起始函数包含可能触发协议使用的条件信息。与关联函数类似，该模型记录了作为起始函数参数的观察概念和协议，但并未具体说明它们是如何组合的。其目的是让不同类型的起始函数采用不同的组合方法。

A similar set of linkages appears at the knowledge level using start functions and outcome functions, as shown in Figure 8.17. A start function contains information on conditions that are likely to trigger the use of a protocol. Following the example of associative functions, the model records the observation concepts and protocols used as arguments to the start function but does not specify how they are combined. The intention is for different kinds of start functions to have different methods for combining them.

图 8.17 知识层面的起始函数和结果函数的使用。

Figure 8.17 The use of start and outcome functions at the knowledge level.

起始函数表示开始执行某个动作的条件，结果 函数表示目标和副作用。

Start functions indicate the conditions for beginning an action, and outcome functions indicate the targets and side effects.

例如，添加润滑油的协议由一个以低油位为参数的启动函数指示。

Example The protocol add oil is indicated by a start function with an argument of low oil level.

例如， β受体阻滞剂可用于治疗高血压和心绞痛，但如果患者患有哮喘则不应使用。这引出了三个起始函数，它们都表示β受体阻滞剂治疗。（β受体阻滞剂治疗是一个资源分配方案，资源类型为β受体阻滞剂。）其中两个起始函数，一个以高血压为参数，另一个以心绞痛为参数，其主体结构简单，无需任何处理，这是一种直接的指示。第三个起始函数以哮喘为参数，其主体结构为逻辑否定。（我们可以有一个中心指示类型的起始函数子类型，但这实际上取决于参数的处理方式。）

Example Beta-blockers are a treatment for hypertension and angina but should not be used if the patient has asthma. This leads to three start functions, all of which indicate beta-blocker treatment. (Beta-blocker treatment is a protocol with a resource allocation of the resource type beta-blocker.) Two start functions, one with the argument hypertension and one with the argument angina, have a simple body with no processing, which is a straightforward indication. The third has the argument asthma and is a body of logical negation. (We could have a centra-indication subtype of start function, but it all really depends on the way the arguments are processed.)

结果函数的运作方式类似。同样，输入是协议和观察概念的组合。结果是两组观察概念。一些观察概念代表协议的目标用途，即体现协议目的的效果。另一些观察概念则是副作用。一个协议可以产生多个结果。这可能反映了患者当时可能存在的其他协议或观察概念。这些结果作为参数引入，继承自知识函数。

Outcome functions operate similarly. Again the input is a combination of protocols and observation concepts. The result is two sets of observation concepts. Some observation concepts represent the target use of the protocol, that is, the effects that represent the purpose of the protocol. The other observation concepts are the side effects. A protocol can have many results. This may reflect other protocols or observation concepts that the patient might have at that time. These are introduced as arguments inherited from the knowledge function.

例如，降低价格的结果函数以增加市场份额为目标，但副作用是降低每单位销售收入。

Example Decreasing prices have an outcome function with a target of increased market share and a side effect of reduced revenue per unit sold.

例如，肝移植方案的结果函数以良好的肝功能为目标，并考虑器官排斥和胆道狭窄（肠管变窄）等副作用。起始函数还可以包含这些情况发生概率的信息。可能存在多个结果函数，它们具有相同的目标和副作用，但参数代表影响手术的疾病。这些不同的结果函数表明，由于疾病参数的存在，目标和副作用的发生概率有所不同。

Example The protocol liver transplant has an outcome function with a target of good liver function and side effects of organ rejection and biliary stricture (narrowing of the bowel duct). The start function can also include information on the likelihoods of these conditions arising. Separate outcome functions might exist with the same target and side effects but with arguments representing diseases that affect the procedure. These separate outcome functions indicate different likelihoods for the target and side effects due to presence of the disease arguments.

参考

References

  2. Cairns, T., A. Casey, M. Fowler, M. Thursz, and H. Timimi. The Cosmos Clinical Process Model. National Health Service, Information Management Centre, 15 Frederick Rd, Birmingham, B15 1JD, England. Report ECBS20A & ECBS20B <http://www.sm.ic.ac.uk/medicine/cpm>, 1992.
  3. IMC.通用基本规范通用模型。英国国家医疗服务体系信息管理中心，1992年。
